applies_to.note: A legally binding sovereign deposit guarantee functioning as deposit insurance may qualify; the presence of insurance alone does not make a deposit stable.

R-LCR40.8-effective-dis-definition.portfolio_relevance: Determines whether the 3%/5% stable treatment is available at all in a jurisdiction; the FDIC satisfies this, so US small banks can use the stable bucket.

R-LCR40.11-stable-deposit-3pct.title: Optional 3% run-off rate for stable deposits with prefunded deposit insurance
R-LCR40.11-stable-deposit-3pct.statement: Jurisdictions may apply a 3% run-off rate to stable deposits where the deposit insurance scheme is prefunded via periodic levies, has assured access to additional funding, and gives depositors rapid access to insured deposits.
R-LCR40.11-stable-deposit-3pct.quote: Jurisdictions may choose to apply a run-off rate of 3% to stable deposits in their jurisdiction, if they meet the above stable deposit criteria and the following additional criteria for deposit insurance schemes:

applies_to.note: National discretion; requires all three deposit-insurance criteria and rapid payout, typically within seven business days.

R-LCR40.11-stable-deposit-3pct.portfolio_relevance: The lowest available deposit outflow factor; a deposit-funded card bank in a qualifying jurisdiction needs 40% less buffer per stable deposit dollar than at 5%.

R-LCR40.12-evidence-for-3pct.title: Jurisdictions applying 3% must evidence sub-3% historical stable-deposit run-off
R-LCR40.12-evidence-for-3pct.statement: Jurisdictions applying the 3% stable-deposit run-off rate should be able to evidence stable-deposit run-off below 3% within the banking system during stress periods consistent with LCR conditions.
R-LCR40.12-evidence-for-3pct.quote: Jurisdictions applying the 3% run-off rate to stable deposits with deposit insurance arrangements that meet the above criteria should be able to provide evidence of run-off rates for stable deposits within the banking system below 3% during any periods of stress experienced that are consistent with the conditions within the LCR.

applies_to.note: Evidential burden sits with the jurisdiction, not the individual bank.

R-LCR40.12-evidence-for-3pct.portfolio_relevance: Explains why most jurisdictions including the US do not use 3%, so 5% is the practical stable-deposit floor for modelling.

R-LCR40.13-less-stable-10pct.title: Less stable retail deposits carry a minimum 10% run-off rate
R-LCR40.13-less-stable-10pct.statement: Supervisors should develop additional buckets for potentially less stable retail deposits with a minimum run-off rate of 10%, covering deposits not fully insured, high-value deposits, deposits of sophisticated or high net worth individuals, rapidly withdrawable deposits and foreign currency deposits.
R-LCR40.13-less-stable-10pct.quote: Supervisory authorities should develop additional buckets with higher run-off rates as necessary to apply to buckets of potentially less stable retail deposits in their jurisdictions, with a minimum run-off rate of 10%.

applies_to.note: Jurisdiction-specific buckets and rates above the 10% floor must be publicly transparent; the US applies higher rates to non-transactional and brokered retail deposits.

R-LCR40.13-less-stable-10pct.portfolio_relevance: Doubles the buffer cost of uninsured or rate-shopping deposits, penalising card banks that fund growth with internet or brokered retail money.

R-LCR40.14-unidentified-deposits-less-st.title: Deposits that cannot be identified as stable must be placed in the less stable bucket
R-LCR40.14-unidentified-deposits-less-st.statement: If a bank cannot readily identify which retail deposits qualify as stable, it must place the full amount in the less stable buckets established by its supervisor.
R-LCR40.14-unidentified-deposits-less-st.quote: If a bank is not able to readily identify which retail deposits would qualify as “stable” according to the above definition (eg the bank cannot determine which deposits are covered by an effective deposit insurance scheme or a sovereign deposit guarantee), it must place the full amount in the “less stable” buckets as established by its supervisor.
R-LCR40.14-unidentified-deposits-less-st.portfolio_relevance: A data-capability penalty: banks without account-level insurance coverage data are forced to the punitive rate, so investment in deposit analytics directly reduces required HQLA.

R-LCR40.16-term-deposit-exclusion.title: Retail term deposits beyond 30 days may be excluded from outflows
R-LCR40.16-term-deposit-exclusion.statement: Retail term deposits with residual maturity or notice period greater than 30 days may be excluded from expected cash outflows where the depositor has no legal right to withdraw within the 30-day horizon, or where early withdrawal triggers a penalty materially greater than the loss of interest.
R-LCR40.16-term-deposit-exclusion.quote: Cash outflows related to retail term deposits with a residual maturity or withdrawal notice period greater than 30 days may be excluded from total expected cash outflows if the depositor has no legal right to withdraw deposits within the 30-day horizon of the LCR, or if early withdrawal results in a significant penalty that is materially greater than the loss of interest.

applies_to.note: Supervisors may nonetheless apply a higher than 0% run-off to such deposits under LCR40.18; any penalty-free withdrawable portion is treated as a demand deposit.

R-LCR40.16-term-deposit-exclusion.portfolio_relevance: The single strongest liability-side lever: lengthening CD maturities past 30 days with real early-withdrawal penalties removes those balances from the denominator entirely.

R-LCR40.17-early-withdrawal-contaminatio.title: Waiving early-withdrawal penalties contaminates the entire term deposit category
R-LCR40.17-early-withdrawal-contaminatio.statement: If a bank allows a depositor to withdraw a term deposit without applying the penalty, or despite a no-withdrawal clause, the entire category of such funds must be treated as demand deposits subject to retail run-off rates.
R-LCR40.17-early-withdrawal-contaminatio.quote: If a bank allows a depositor to withdraw such deposits without applying the corresponding penalty, or despite a clause that says the depositor has no legal right to withdraw, the entire category of these funds must be treated as demand deposits

applies_to.note: Supervisors may define hardship exceptions that do not contaminate the pool.

R-LCR40.17-early-withdrawal-contaminatio.portfolio_relevance: Imposes a portfolio-wide cliff cost on customer-friendly CD break practices, so a restructuring toward term funding must be contractually enforced to count.

R-LCR40.22-small-business-as-retail.title: Small business customer funding treated the same as retail deposits
R-LCR40.22-small-business-as-retail.statement: Unsecured wholesale funding provided by small business customers is treated the same way as retail deposits, using the same stable and less stable bucket definitions and run-off factors.
R-LCR40.22-small-business-as-retail.quote: Unsecured wholesale funding provided by small business customers is treated the same way as retail deposits for the purposes of this standard, effectively distinguishing between a "stable" portion of funding provided by small business customers and different buckets of less stable funding defined by each jurisdiction. The same bucket definitions and associated run-off factors apply as for retail deposits.
R-LCR40.22-small-business-as-retail.portfolio_relevance: Lets small business deposit funding be modelled with retail run-off rates, a material relief for community banks funding SME card and line products.

R-LCR40.23-small-business-1m-threshold.title: Small business customer defined by CRE30 retail management and a EUR 1 million aggregate funding limit
R-LCR40.23-small-business-1m-threshold.statement: Small business customers are defined in line with the CRE30.20 to CRE30.22 definition of small business loans managed as retail exposures, provided total aggregated funding raised from that customer is less than EUR 1 million on a consolidated basis.
R-LCR40.23-small-business-1m-threshold.quote: "Small business customers" are defined in line with the definition of loans extended to small businesses in CRE30.20 to CRE30.22 that are managed as retail exposures and are generally considered as having similar liquidity risk characteristics to retail accounts provided the total aggregated funding raised from one small business customer is less than €1 million (on a consolidated basis where applicable).

applies_to.note: Aggregated funding is gross across all funding forms, and affiliated customers may be treated as a single creditor.

R-LCR40.23-small-business-1m-threshold.portfolio_relevance: Sets the exact size threshold at which business deposits fall out of retail treatment and jump from 5-10% to 40% run-off, a hard boundary for deposit-gathering strategy.

R-LCR40.26-operational-deposit-25pct.title: Qualifying operational deposits receive a 25% run-off factor
R-LCR40.26-operational-deposit-25pct.statement: Deposits placed to facilitate clearing, custody or cash management activities may receive a 25% run-off factor only where the customer has a substantive dependency on the bank and the deposit is required for those activities.
R-LCR40.26-operational-deposit-25pct.quote: These funds may receive a 25% run-off factor only if the customer has a substantive dependency with the bank and the deposit is required for such activities.

applies_to.note: Supervisory approval required, and supervisors may refuse the treatment where operational deposits are concentrated in few customers.

R-LCR40.26-operational-deposit-25pct.portfolio_relevance: Halves the outflow on qualifying corporate balances versus the 40%/100% defaults, rewarding treasury-services relationships over rate-driven corporate deposits.

R-LCR40.29-excess-balances-excluded.title: Excess balances above operational need do not qualify for the 25% factor
R-LCR40.29-excess-balances-excluded.statement: Balances that could be withdrawn while still leaving enough funds for the clearing, custody and cash management activities do not qualify for the 25% factor and must be treated as non-operational; if the excess cannot be determined, the whole deposit is non-operational.
R-LCR40.29-excess-balances-excluded.quote: Any excess balances that could be withdrawn and would still leave enough funds to fulfil these clearing, custody and cash management activities do not qualify for the 25% factor.
R-LCR40.29-excess-balances-excluded.portfolio_relevance: Another data-capability penalty: without a documented excess-balance methodology the whole balance runs at 40% or 100%.

R-LCR40.36-insured-operational-as-stable.title: Insured portion of operational deposits treated as stable retail deposits
R-LCR40.36-insured-operational-as-stable.statement: The portion of operational deposits from clearing, custody and cash management activities that is fully covered by deposit insurance may receive the same treatment as stable retail deposits.
R-LCR40.36-insured-operational-as-stable.quote: The portion of the operational deposits generated by clearing, custody and cash management activities that is fully covered by deposit insurance may receive the same treatment as “stable” retail deposits.
R-LCR40.36-insured-operational-as-stable.portfolio_relevance: Converts insured operational balances from a 25% to a 5% outflow, materially favouring small-ticket insured business operating accounts.

R-LCR40.40-corporate-40pct.title: Non-operational non-financial corporate, sovereign, MDB and PSE funding runs off at 40%
R-LCR40.40-corporate-40pct.statement: Deposits and other unsecured funding from non-financial corporates that are not small business customers, and from sovereigns, central banks, MDBs and PSEs, that are not held for operational purposes carry a 40% run-off factor unless the LCR40.41 insurance criteria are met.
R-LCR40.40-corporate-40pct.quote: This category comprises all deposits and other extensions of unsecured funding from non-financial corporate customers (that are not categorised as small business customers) and (both domestic and foreign) sovereign, central bank, multilateral development bank, and public sector entity (PSE) customers that are not specifically held for operational purposes (as defined above). The run-off factor for these funds must be 40%, unless the criteria in LCR40.41 are met.
R-LCR40.40-corporate-40pct.portfolio_relevance: Prices non-operational corporate and municipal deposits at eight times the stable retail rate, penalising banks that fund lending growth with large public-entity balances.

R-LCR40.41-corporate-insured-20pct.title: Fully insured non-financial corporate and public sector funding runs off at 20%
R-LCR40.41-corporate-insured-20pct.statement: Unsecured wholesale funding from non-financial corporates, sovereigns, central banks, MDBs and PSEs without operational relationships may receive a 20% run-off factor where the entire deposit is fully covered by an effective deposit insurance scheme or equivalent public guarantee.
R-LCR40.41-corporate-insured-20pct.quote: Unsecured wholesale funding provided by non-financial corporate customers, sovereigns, central banks, multilateral development banks and PSEs without operational relationships may receive a 20% run-off factor if the entire amount of the deposit is fully covered by an effective deposit insurance scheme or by a public guarantee that provides equivalent protection.

applies_to.note: Requires the entire amount to be covered, not just the portion up to the insurance limit.

R-LCR40.41-corporate-insured-20pct.portfolio_relevance: Halves the corporate deposit outflow when fully insured, making sub-limit business deposits distinctly cheaper funding for a card lender.

R-LCR40.42-financial-institutions-100pct.title: Non-operational funding from financial institutions and other entities runs off at 100%
R-LCR40.42-financial-institutions-100pct.statement: Deposits and other funding from banks, securities firms, insurers, fiduciaries, beneficiaries, conduits, SPVs, affiliates and other entities not held for operational purposes carry a 100% run-off factor.
R-LCR40.42-financial-institutions-100pct.quote: This category consists of all deposits and other funding from other institutions (including banks, securities firms, insurance companies, etc), fiduciaries, beneficiaries, conduits and special purpose vehicles, affiliated entities of the bank and other entities that are not specifically held for operational purposes (as defined above) and not included in the prior three categories. The run-off factor for these funds must be 100%.

applies_to.note: Affiliate funding is included unless it is operational, in a cooperative network, or from a non-financial corporate affiliate.

R-LCR40.42-financial-institutions-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Assumes total loss of financial-sector funding, so a card bank funded by wholesale bank lines or ABS conduits must hold HQLA equal to the full balance.

R-LCR40.43-retail-held-debt-securities.title: Bank-issued debt securities treated as wholesale unless restricted to retail holders
R-LCR40.43-retail-held-debt-securities.statement: All notes, bonds and other debt securities issued by the bank must be treated in the 100% wholesale category regardless of holder, unless the bond is sold exclusively in the retail market and held in retail or small business accounts with contractual limitations preventing other parties from holding it.
R-LCR40.43-retail-held-debt-securities.quote: All notes, bonds and other debt securities issued by the bank must be included in this category regardless of the holder, unless the bond is sold exclusively in the retail market and held in retail accounts (including small business customer accounts treated as retail per LCR40.22 to LCR40.24), in which case the instruments may be treated in the appropriate retail or small business customer deposit category.

applies_to.note: Marketing to retail is not sufficient; contractual holding restrictions are required.

R-LCR40.43-retail-held-debt-securities.portfolio_relevance: Blocks reclassifying wholesale-funded issuance as cheap retail funding, constraining a card bank's ability to term out via retail-branded notes.

R-LCR40.47-secured-funding-level1-0pct.title: Secured funding backed by Level 1 assets or with the domestic central bank runs off at 0%; Level 2 at the asset haircut
R-LCR40.47-secured-funding-level1-0pct.statement: Maturing secured funding backed by Level 1 assets, and any maturing secured funding with the bank's domestic central bank, is assumed not to run off, while secured funding backed by Level 2 assets runs off by the amount of the applicable haircut.
R-LCR40.47-secured-funding-level1-0pct.quote: Due to the high quality of Level 1 assets, no reduction in funding availability against these assets is assumed to occur. Moreover, no reduction in funding availability is expected for any maturing secured funding transactions with the bank’s domestic central bank. A reduction in funding availability must be assigned to maturing transactions backed by Level 2 assets equivalent to the required haircuts.

applies_to.note: A 25% factor may apply to transactions with the domestic sovereign, MDBs or 20%-or-lower risk weighted domestic PSEs backed by other collateral.

R-LCR40.47-secured-funding-level1-0pct.portfolio_relevance: Repo funded against Treasuries is treated as fully rollable, so collateral quality directly determines whether secured borrowing is a liquidity liability or a neutral.

R-LCR40.48-secured-funding-100pct.title: All other maturing secured funding runs off at 100%
R-LCR40.48-secured-funding-100pct.statement: For all maturing secured funding transactions not otherwise categorised, the run-off factor is 100%, including transactions where the bank has satisfied customer short positions with its own long inventory.
R-LCR40.48-secured-funding-100pct.quote: For all other maturing transactions the run-off factor is 100%, including transactions where a bank has satisfied customers’ short positions with its own long inventory.

applies_to.note: Table in the paragraph gives 0% Level 1, 15% Level 2A, 25% eligible RMBS, 50% other Level 2B, 100% all others.

R-LCR40.48-secured-funding-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Secured borrowing against loan collateral (eg card receivables pledged to a facility) is assumed to disappear entirely within 30 days, requiring full HQLA cover.

R-LCR40.51-downgrade-trigger-100pct.title: 100% outflow for collateral or cash triggered by up to a 3-notch downgrade
R-LCR40.51-downgrade-trigger-100pct.statement: Banks must assume 100% of the additional collateral or cash outflow arising from any downgrade up to and including a three-notch downgrade of the bank's long-term credit rating.
R-LCR40.51-downgrade-trigger-100pct.quote: Increased liquidity needs related to downgrade triggers embedded in financing transactions, derivatives and other contracts: 100% of the amount of collateral that would be posted for, or contractual cash outflows associated with, any downgrade up to and including a 3-notch downgrade.

applies_to.note: Short-term rating triggers are mapped to the corresponding long-term rating.

R-LCR40.51-downgrade-trigger-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Penalises rating-sensitive contractual structures, including securitisation trust triggers on card master trusts that require reserve funding on downgrade.

R-LCR40.57-abs-covered-bond-100pct.title: 100% outflow on bank-issued ABS, covered bonds and structured financing maturing within 30 days
R-LCR40.57-abs-covered-bond-100pct.statement: Funding transactions in asset-backed securities, covered bonds and other structured financing instruments issued by the bank itself and maturing within the 30-day period must be assumed to run off at 100%, on the assumption the refinancing market does not exist.
R-LCR40.57-abs-covered-bond-100pct.quote: Loss of funding on asset-backed securities, covered bonds and other structured financing instruments: 100% outflow of funding transactions maturing within the 30-day period, when these instruments are issued by the bank itself (as this assumes that the re-financing market will not exist).

applies_to.note: The outflow may be offset against HQLA becoming unencumbered on maturity of the instrument.

R-LCR40.57-abs-covered-bond-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Directly penalises credit card master trust term ABS amortising within 30 days: securitising card receivables converts deposits into a funding source assumed to vanish completely.

R-LCR40.58-abcp-conduit-100pct.title: 100% of maturing amount and 100% of returnable assets for ABCP and conduit financing
R-LCR40.58-abcp-conduit-100pct.statement: For asset-backed commercial paper, conduits, securities investment vehicles and similar facilities, banks must assume 100% of the maturing amount plus 100% of assets that could be returned under embedded options or liquidity puts within the 30-day period.
R-LCR40.58-abcp-conduit-100pct.quote: Loss of funding on asset-backed commercial paper, conduits, securities investment vehicles and other such financing facilities: 100% of maturing amount and 100% of returnable assets.

applies_to.note: Look-through to the SPE is required irrespective of whether it is consolidated.

R-LCR40.58-abcp-conduit-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Makes conduit funding of card or dealer receivables the most expensive funding form in the LCR, effectively double-charging maturing paper and returnable assets.

R-LCR40.59-facility-definition.title: Definition of credit and liquidity facilities; unconditionally revocable facilities excluded
R-LCR40.59-facility-definition.statement: Credit and liquidity facilities are explicit contractual agreements to extend funds at a future date to retail or wholesale counterparties, and include only contractually irrevocable (committed) or conditionally revocable agreements; facilities unconditionally cancellable by the bank are excluded from this section and fall under other contingent funding obligations in LCR40.67.
R-LCR40.59-facility-definition.quote: credit and liquidity facilities are defined as explicit contractual agreements or obligations to extend funds at a future date to retail or wholesale counterparties. These facilities only include contractually irrevocable (committed) or conditionally revocable agreements to extend funds in the future. Unconditionally revocable facilities that are unconditionally cancellable by the bank (in particular, those without a precondition of a material change in the credit condition of the borrower) are excluded from this section and included in LCR40.67.

applies_to.note: This is the pivotal classification for credit cards: US card lines are typically unconditionally cancellable and therefore fall to LCR40.67/LCR40.73 national-discretion rates rather than the 5% committed rate.

R-LCR40.59-facility-definition.portfolio_relevance: Determines whether an unused credit card line attracts the prescribed 5% drawdown or a nationally-set rate, and therefore whether making card lines cancellable is a liquidity-optimal contract design.

R-LCR40.59-drawn-facilities-not-repaid.title: Facilities assumed drawn must be assumed to remain outstanding without repayment
R-LCR40.59-drawn-facilities-not-repaid.statement: All facilities assumed to be drawn in the scenario must be assumed to remain outstanding without repayment regardless of their maturity.
R-LCR40.59-drawn-facilities-not-repaid.quote: Therefore, all facilities that are assumed to be drawn (as outlined in the paragraphs below) must be assumed to remain outstanding without repayment, regardless of maturity.
R-LCR40.59-drawn-facilities-not-repaid.portfolio_relevance: Blocks netting a short-dated facility drawdown against its own repayment, so short-tenor card or working-capital lines get no relief for fast turnover.

R-LCR40.60-netting-posted-hqla.title: Undrawn facility amounts may be netted against HQLA collateral posted by the counterparty
R-LCR40.60-netting-posted-hqla.statement: The undrawn portion of a facility may be calculated net of HQLA already posted, or contractually required to be posted, as collateral by the counterparty, provided the bank can legally and operationally re-use the collateral and there is no undue correlation between drawdown probability and collateral value.
R-LCR40.60-netting-posted-hqla.quote: The currently undrawn portion of these facilities may be calculated net of any HQLA eligible for the stock of HQLA, if the HQLA have already been posted as collateral by the counterparty to secure the facilities

applies_to.note: Collateral may only be netted to the extent it is not already counted in the HQLA stock.

R-LCR40.60-netting-posted-hqla.portfolio_relevance: Gives a concrete mitigation: secured or cash-collateralised card and business lines carry a smaller undrawn balance in the outflow calculation.

R-LCR40.61-liquidity-facility-definition.title: Definition of a liquidity facility as a backstop for customer debt refinancing
R-LCR40.61-liquidity-facility-definition.statement: A liquidity facility is a committed undrawn backup facility used to refinance a customer's debt obligations where the customer cannot roll that debt in financial markets, measured as the customer's outstanding debt maturing within 30 days that the facility backstops.
R-LCR40.61-liquidity-facility-definition.quote: A liquidity facility is defined as any committed, undrawn backup facility that would be utilised to refinance the debt obligations of a customer in situations where such a customer is unable to rollover that debt in financial markets (eg pursuant to a commercial paper programme, secured financing transactions, obligations to redeem units).

applies_to.note: Any remaining commitment beyond the backstopped maturing debt is treated as a committed credit facility with the LCR40.64 drawdown rate.

R-LCR40.61-liquidity-facility-definition.portfolio_relevance: Separates the 30% liquidity-facility rate from the 10% credit-facility rate for corporate commitments, so how a commitment is documented changes its liquidity charge threefold.

R-LCR40.61-working-capital-is-credit-fac.title: General working capital and revolving corporate facilities are credit, not liquidity, facilities
R-LCR40.61-working-capital-is-credit-fac.statement: General working capital facilities for corporate entities, including revolving credit facilities for general corporate or working capital purposes, must not be classified as liquidity facilities but as credit facilities.
R-LCR40.61-working-capital-is-credit-fac.quote: General working capital facilities for corporate entities (eg revolving credit facilities in place for general corporate or working capital purposes) must not be classified as liquidity facilities, but as credit facilities.
R-LCR40.61-working-capital-is-credit-fac.portfolio_relevance: Confirms that ordinary revolving business lines attract the 10% rather than 30% drawdown, an important classification for community bank commercial revolvers.

R-LCR40.64-all-drawdowns-reflected.title: All contractual and estimated drawdowns within 30 days must be reflected as outflows
R-LCR40.64-all-drawdowns-reflected.statement: Any contractual loan drawdowns from committed facilities and estimated drawdowns from revocable facilities within the 30-day period must be fully reflected as cash outflows.
R-LCR40.64-all-drawdowns-reflected.quote: Any contractual loan drawdowns from committed facilities and estimated drawdowns from revocable facilities within the 30-day period must be fully reflected as outflows.
R-LCR40.64-all-drawdowns-reflected.portfolio_relevance: Extends the drawdown charge to revocable facilities on an estimated basis, so even cancellable card lines cannot be assumed to generate zero draw.

R-LCR40.64-retail-sme-5pct-drawdown.title: 5% drawdown on undrawn committed credit and liquidity facilities to retail and small business customers
R-LCR40.64-retail-sme-5pct-drawdown.statement: Banks must assume a 5% drawdown of the undrawn portion of committed credit and liquidity facilities extended to retail and small business customers.
R-LCR40.64-retail-sme-5pct-drawdown.quote: (1) Committed credit and liquidity facilities to retail and small business customers: banks must assume a 5% drawdown of the undrawn portion of these facilities.

applies_to.note: Applies only where the facility is committed (irrevocable) or conditionally revocable per LCR40.59; unconditionally cancellable card lines fall to LCR40.73 national discretion. US LCR applies the 5% rate to retail committed lines for covered firms.

R-LCR40.64-retail-sme-5pct-drawdown.portfolio_relevance: This is the headline credit card constraint: every dollar of unused committed card line adds five cents to 30-day outflow, so cutting or making revocable unused open-to-buy is the cheapest LCR improvement available to a card lender.

R-LCR40.64-corporate-credit-10pct.title: 10% drawdown on committed credit facilities to non-financial corporates, sovereigns, PSEs and MDBs
R-LCR40.64-corporate-credit-10pct.statement: Banks must assume a 10% drawdown of the undrawn portion of committed credit facilities to non-financial corporates, sovereigns and central banks, PSEs and multilateral development banks.
R-LCR40.64-corporate-credit-10pct.quote: (2) Committed credit facilities to non-financial corporates, sovereigns and central banks, PSEs and multilateral development banks: banks must assume a 10% drawdown of the undrawn portion of these credit facilities.
R-LCR40.64-corporate-credit-10pct.portfolio_relevance: Corporate revolvers cost twice as much liquidity per undrawn dollar as retail card lines, tilting a constrained bank toward retail commitment growth.

R-LCR40.64-corporate-liquidity-30pct.title: 30% drawdown on committed liquidity facilities to non-financial corporates, sovereigns, PSEs and MDBs
R-LCR40.64-corporate-liquidity-30pct.statement: Banks must assume a 30% drawdown of the undrawn portion of committed liquidity facilities to non-financial corporates, sovereigns and central banks, PSEs and multilateral development banks.
R-LCR40.64-corporate-liquidity-30pct.quote: (3) Committed liquidity facilities to non-financial corporates, sovereigns and central banks, PSEs and multilateral development banks: banks must assume a 30% drawdown of the undrawn portion of these liquidity facilities.
R-LCR40.64-corporate-liquidity-30pct.portfolio_relevance: Backstop lines for municipal or corporate debt programmes are six times as liquidity-expensive as retail card lines per undrawn dollar.

R-LCR40.64-bank-facilities-40pct.title: 40% drawdown on committed credit and liquidity facilities to prudentially supervised banks
R-LCR40.64-bank-facilities-40pct.statement: Banks must assume a 40% drawdown of the undrawn portion of committed credit and liquidity facilities extended to banks subject to prudential supervision.
R-LCR40.64-bank-facilities-40pct.quote: (4) Committed credit and liquidity facilities extended to banks subject to prudential supervision: banks must assume a 40% drawdown of the undrawn portion of these facilities.
R-LCR40.64-bank-facilities-40pct.portfolio_relevance: Discourages interbank commitment provision, which is eight times the retail rate per undrawn dollar.

R-LCR40.64-other-fi-credit-40pct.title: 40% drawdown on committed credit facilities to other financial institutions
R-LCR40.64-other-fi-credit-40pct.statement: Banks must assume a 40% drawdown of the undrawn portion of committed credit facilities to other financial institutions, including securities firms, insurance companies, fiduciaries and beneficiaries.
R-LCR40.64-other-fi-credit-40pct.quote: (5) Committed credit facilities to other financial institutions, including securities firms, insurance companies, fiduciaries, and beneficiaries: banks must assume a 40% drawdown of the undrawn portion of these credit facilities.
R-LCR40.64-other-fi-credit-40pct.portfolio_relevance: Prices warehouse and subscription lines to non-bank lenders at eight times retail card lines, a direct constraint on banks financing fintech card issuers.

R-LCR40.64-other-fi-liquidity-100pct.title: 100% drawdown on committed liquidity facilities to other financial institutions
R-LCR40.64-other-fi-liquidity-100pct.statement: Banks must assume a 100% drawdown of the undrawn portion of committed liquidity facilities to other financial institutions including securities firms, insurance companies, fiduciaries and beneficiaries.
R-LCR40.64-other-fi-liquidity-100pct.quote: (6) Committed liquidity facilities to other financial institutions, including securities firms, insurance companies' fiduciaries and beneficiaries: banks must assume a 100% drawdown of the undrawn portion of these liquidity facilities.
R-LCR40.64-other-fi-liquidity-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Full-value HQLA cover required, effectively prohibiting undrawn liquidity backstops to financial firms for a liquidity-constrained bank.

R-LCR40.64-other-legal-entities-100pct.title: 100% drawdown on committed facilities to SPEs, conduits and other legal entities
R-LCR40.64-other-legal-entities-100pct.statement: Banks must assume a 100% drawdown of the undrawn portion of committed credit and liquidity facilities to other legal entities including SPEs, conduits and special purpose vehicles.
R-LCR40.64-other-legal-entities-100pct.quote: (7) Committed credit and liquidity facilities to other legal entities (including SPEs as defined in LCR40.58, conduits and special purpose vehicles, and other entities not included in the prior categories): Banks must assume a 100% drawdown of the undrawn portion of these facilities.

applies_to.note: Facilities to hedge funds, money market funds and special purpose funding vehicles are captured in their entirety as liquidity facilities to other legal entities.

R-LCR40.64-other-legal-entities-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Liquidity support to a bank's own card securitisation vehicle is charged at full face value, cancelling much of the funding benefit of securitising card receivables.

R-LCR40.64-committed-means-irrevocable.title: Committed facilities means irrevocable facilities
R-LCR40.64-committed-means-irrevocable.statement: For the purposes of the drawdown rates, committed facilities are those which are irrevocable.
R-LCR40.64-committed-means-irrevocable.quote: Committed facilities refer to those which are irrevocable. The potential liquidity risks associated with the bank's own structured financing facilities must be treated according to LCR40.57
R-LCR40.64-committed-means-irrevocable.portfolio_relevance: The one-line test separating the 5% retail commitment charge from the national-discretion treatment of cancellable card lines.

R-LCR40.65-lending-to-fi-100pct.title: 100% outflow on contractual lending obligations to financial institutions
R-LCR40.65-lending-to-fi-100pct.statement: Any contractual lending obligations to financial institutions, including central banks, not captured elsewhere must be treated as a 100% outflow.
R-LCR40.65-lending-to-fi-100pct.quote: Any contractual lending obligations to financial institutions, including central banks, not captured elsewhere in this standard must be captured here at a 100% outflow rate.
R-LCR40.65-lending-to-fi-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Any committed forward lending to financial counterparties consumes HQLA one-for-one.

R-LCR40.66-50pct-lending-obligation-test.title: Contractual lending obligations to retail and non-financial clients above 50% of contractual inflows create a 100% outflow
R-LCR40.66-50pct-lending-obligation-test.statement: Where total contractual obligations to extend funds to retail and non-financial wholesale clients within 30 days, not captured elsewhere, exceed 50% of total contractual inflows due from those clients in the same period, the excess must be reported as a 100% outflow.
R-LCR40.66-50pct-lending-obligation-test.quote: If the total of all contractual obligations to extend funds to retail and non- financial wholesale (eg including small or medium-sized entities and other corporates, sovereigns, multilateral development banks and PSEs) clients within the next 30 calendar days (not captured in the prior categories) exceeds 50% of the total contractual inflows due in the next 30 calendar days from these clients, the difference must be reported as a 100% outflow.

applies_to.note: Applies only to obligations not already captured in the LCR40.64 facility categories.

R-LCR40.66-50pct-lending-obligation-test.portfolio_relevance: A relative-size test that penalises a rapidly growing lender whose forward lending commitments outpace scheduled repayments from the same client base.

R-LCR40.67-other-contingent-national-dis.title: Run-off rates for other contingent funding obligations set at national discretion
R-LCR40.67-other-contingent-national-dis.statement: Run-off rates for other contingent funding obligations are set at national discretion, with supervisors determining the liquidity risk impact and required HQLA and disclosing the assigned rates publicly.
R-LCR40.67-other-contingent-national-dis.quote: Other contingent funding obligations: (run-off rates at national discretion). National supervisors may work with supervised institutions in their jurisdictions to determine the liquidity risk impact of these contingent liabilities and the resulting stock of HQLA that should accordingly be maintained.

applies_to.note: Explicit national-discretion gate; this is the bucket into which unconditionally cancellable credit card lines fall.

R-LCR40.67-other-contingent-national-dis.portfolio_relevance: For US card issuers, whose lines are typically unconditionally cancellable, the applicable drawdown rate is set by the US rule rather than Basel, so any evaluation must apply the domestic overlay.

R-LCR40.71-trade-finance-5pct.title: Trade finance contingent obligations may receive a run-off rate of 5% or less
R-LCR40.71-trade-finance-5pct.statement: For contingent funding obligations from trade finance instruments such as documentary letters of credit, collections, import and export bills and trade-related guarantees, national authorities may apply a relatively low run-off rate of 5% or less.
R-LCR40.71-trade-finance-5pct.quote: In the case of contingent funding obligations stemming from trade finance instruments, national authorities may apply a relatively low run-off rate (eg 5% or less).

applies_to.note: National discretion on the exact rate; direct import or export financing lending commitments are excluded and take the LCR40.64 rates.

R-LCR40.71-trade-finance-5pct.portfolio_relevance: Trade-related contingents are the cheapest off-balance sheet exposure in the LCR, favouring trade finance over general revolving commitments for a constrained bank.

R-LCR40.73-uncommitted-revocable-facilit.title: Unconditionally revocable uncommitted credit and liquidity facilities are other contingent funding obligations at nationally set rates
R-LCR40.73-uncommitted-revocable-facilit.statement: National authorities must set run-off rates for other contingent funding obligations, which include unconditionally revocable uncommitted credit and liquidity facilities.
R-LCR40.73-uncommitted-revocable-facilit.quote: National authorities must determine the run-off rates for the other contingent funding obligations listed below in accordance with LCR40.67. Other contingent funding obligations include products and instruments such as: (1) unconditionally revocable “uncommitted” credit and liquidity facilities;

applies_to.note: This is where unused credit card lines that are unconditionally cancellable by the bank are captured; the applied rate is jurisdictional, not Basel-prescribed.

R-LCR40.73-uncommitted-revocable-facilit.portfolio_relevance: The decisive rule for credit card portfolios: unused card lines only escape the 5% committed charge if unconditionally cancellable, and even then attract a domestically-set run-off, so the optimiser must treat the card drawdown factor as a jurisdiction parameter.

R-LCR40.74-other-contractual-outflows-10.title: Other contractual cash outflows at 100%
R-LCR40.74-other-contractual-outflows-10.statement: Any other contractual cash outflows within the next 30 calendar days, such as unsecured collateral borrowings, uncovered short positions, dividends or contractual interest payments, must be captured at 100%; operating cost outflows are excluded.
R-LCR40.74-other-contractual-outflows-10.quote: Other contractual cash outflows: 100%. Any other contractual cash outflows within the next 30 calendar days must be captured in this standard, such as outflows to cover unsecured collateral borrowings, uncovered short positions, dividends or contractual interest payments.
R-LCR40.74-other-contractual-outflows-10.portfolio_relevance: Includes contractual interest and declared dividends, so a card bank's dividend and debt-service schedule directly consumes buffer.

R-LCR40.75-performing-inflows-only.title: Only fully performing exposures may generate cash inflows
R-LCR40.75-performing-inflows-only.statement: A bank may only include contractual inflows, including interest, from outstanding exposures that are fully performing and for which it has no reason to expect default within the 30-day horizon; contingent inflows must be excluded.
R-LCR40.75-performing-inflows-only.quote: the bank must only include contractual inflows (including interest payments) from outstanding exposures that are fully performing and for which the bank has no reason to expect a default within the 30-day time horizon.
R-LCR40.75-performing-inflows-only.portfolio_relevance: Delinquent card balances stop contributing inflow, so credit deterioration in a card book worsens the LCR independently of the capital charge.

R-LCR40.77-inflow-cap-75pct.title: Inflows capped at 75% of outflows, implying a minimum HQLA of 25% of gross outflows
R-LCR40.77-inflow-cap-75pct.statement: The amount of inflows that can offset outflows is capped at 75% of total expected cash outflows, requiring the bank to hold HQLA of at least 25% of total cash outflows.
R-LCR40.77-inflow-cap-75pct.quote: the amount of inflows that can offset outflows must be capped at 75% of total expected cash outflows as calculated in the standard. This requires that a bank must maintain a minimum amount of stock of HQLA equal to 25% of the total cash outflows.

applies_to.note: Basel binds internationally active banks; the US LCR (12 CFR 249) applies only to Category I-IV firms (broadly >= $100bn assets), so small North American banks are outside the binding scope and this is a shadow/benchmark metric for them.

numeric_values: minimum HQLA of 25% of total cash outflows
R-LCR40.77-inflow-cap-75pct.portfolio_relevance: Hard floor on the buffer: even a bank whose card receipts exceed its stressed outflows must still hold HQLA equal to a quarter of gross outflows, so loan repayment cash flow can never fully substitute for securities.

R-LCR40.82-no-inflow-from-own-facilities.title: Zero inflow from credit, liquidity and contingent facilities the bank holds at other institutions
R-LCR40.82-no-inflow-from-own-facilities.statement: No credit, liquidity or other contingent funding facilities the bank holds at other institutions for its own purposes may be assumed drawable; such facilities receive a 0% inflow rate.
R-LCR40.82-no-inflow-from-own-facilities.quote: No credit facilities, liquidity facilities or other contingent funding facilities that the bank holds at other institutions for its own purposes are assumed to be able to be drawn. Such facilities must receive a 0% inflow rate
R-LCR40.82-no-inflow-from-own-facilities.portfolio_relevance: Correspondent bank lines and FHLB availability give no LCR credit, so a small bank cannot substitute committed borrowing capacity for HQLA.

R-LCR40.84-revolving-undrawn-as-committe.title: Revolving credit facilities: assume rollover of drawn balance and treat undrawn balance as a committed facility
R-LCR40.84-revolving-undrawn-as-committe.statement: Inflows may only be taken from fully performing loans at the latest contractual date, and for revolving credit facilities the bank must assume the existing loan is rolled over while any remaining undrawn balance is treated as a committed facility under LCR40.64.
R-LCR40.84-revolving-undrawn-as-committe.quote: When considering loan payments, the bank must only include inflows from fully performing loans. Further, inflows must only be taken at the latest possible date, based on the contractual rights available to counterparties. For revolving credit facilities, a bank must assume that the existing loan is rolled over and that any remaining undrawn balances are treated in the same way as a committed facility according to LCR40.64.
numeric_values: LCR40.64 drawdown rate on the undrawn balance
R-LCR40.84-revolving-undrawn-as-committe.portfolio_relevance: The most punitive rule for credit cards: drawn card balances generate no repayment inflow because they are assumed to roll, while the unused line simultaneously generates a drawdown outflow, so a card portfolio is pure denominator with no offset.

R-LCR40.85-open-maturity-loans-excluded.title: Open-maturity and 30-day-terminable loans generate no inflow except contractual minimum payments
R-LCR40.85-open-maturity-loans-excluded.statement: Inflows from loans with no specific or open maturity must be excluded, as must inflows above the regular amortisation schedule on loans terminable within 30 days, except that contractual minimum payments of principal, fee or interest due within 30 days may be included at the LCR40.86 and LCR40.87 rates.
R-LCR40.85-open-maturity-loans-excluded.quote: Inflows from loans that have no specific maturity (ie have non-defined or open maturity) must be excluded; therefore, a bank must not make assumptions as to when maturity of such loans would occur. This treatment must also apply to loans that can be contractually terminated within 30 days, as any inflows exceeding those according the regular amortisation schedule would be “contingent” (in terms of a possible cancellation of the loan) in nature. As an exception to this approach, banks may include minimum payments of principal, fee or interest associated with an open maturity loan, provided that such payments are contractually due within 30 days.

applies_to.note: The minimum-payment exception is the only route by which a revolving card balance produces any LCR inflow.

R-LCR40.85-open-maturity-loans-excluded.portfolio_relevance: Restricts credit card inflow to the contractual minimum payment, which for a typical US card is roughly 1-3% of the balance, and then only at the 50% retail inflow rate.

R-LCR40.86-retail-inflow-50pct.title: 50% inflow rate on fully performing retail and small business loan payments
R-LCR40.86-retail-inflow-50pct.statement: Payments including interest and instalments from fully performing retail and small business customers contractually due within 30 days generate inflows, but banks must assume continued lending at 50% of contractual inflows, giving a net 50% inflow.
R-LCR40.86-retail-inflow-50pct.quote: All payments (including interest payments and instalments) from retail and small business customers that are fully performing and contractually due within a 30- day horizon may result in inflows. However, banks must assume to continue to extend loans to retail and small business customers, at a rate of 50% of contractual inflows. This results in an inflow of 50% of the contractual amount.

applies_to.note: Basel binds internationally active banks; the US LCR (12 CFR 249) applies only to Category I-IV firms (broadly >= $100bn assets), so small North American banks are outside the binding scope and this is a shadow/benchmark metric for them.

R-LCR40.86-retail-inflow-50pct.portfolio_relevance: Halves the benefit of a fast-amortising retail book: the card minimum payments that do qualify are counted at only 50 cents on the dollar, and are then subject to the 75% aggregate inflow cap.

R-LCR40.87-wholesale-inflow-rates.title: Wholesale inflow rates: 100% from financial institutions and central banks, 50% from non-financial wholesale
R-LCR40.87-wholesale-inflow-rates.statement: Banks must assume continued lending at 0% for financial institutions and central banks and 50% for all other wholesale counterparties, giving inflow rates of 100% for financial institution and central bank counterparties and 50% for non-financial wholesale counterparties.
R-LCR40.87-wholesale-inflow-rates.quote: Banks must assume to continue to extend loans to wholesale clients, at a rate of 0% of inflows for financial institutions and central banks, and 50% for all others, including non-financial corporates, sovereigns, multilateral development banks, and PSEs.
numeric_values: 100% inflow from financial institutions and central banks
R-LCR40.87-wholesale-inflow-rates.portfolio_relevance: Interbank placements return in full while corporate loan repayments count at half, favouring holding surplus liquidity at banks over short corporate lending.

R-LCR40.88-hqla-maturities-not-inflows.title: Maturing HQLA counted in the stock must not also be counted as inflows
R-LCR40.88-hqla-maturities-not-inflows.statement: Level 1 and Level 2 assets maturing within 30 days that meet the operational and definitional requirements must be included in the stock of liquid assets and must not be counted as inflows; non-HQLA securities maturing within 30 days may be treated as 100% inflows.
R-LCR40.88-hqla-maturities-not-inflows.quote: Level 1 and Level 2 assets maturing within 30 days must be included in the stock of liquid assets and must not be considered as inflows

applies_to.note: Payments from Level 1 and Level 2 assets that fail the operational requirements may be counted as inflows.

R-LCR40.88-hqla-maturities-not-inflows.portfolio_relevance: Forces a choice between counting a short-dated security in the numerator or as an inflow, which matters when a small bank's buffer is mostly short Treasuries.

R-CRE20.1-sa-rwa-net-of-provisions.title: Standardised RWA = risk weight x exposure, net of specific provisions
R-CRE20.1-sa-rwa-net-of-provisions.statement: Under the standardised approach, risk-weighted assets equal the standardised risk weight multiplied by the exposure amount, and exposures should be risk-weighted net of specific provisions including partial write-offs.
R-CRE20.1-sa-rwa-net-of-provisions.quote: Risk weighted assets are calculated as the product of the standardised risk weights and the exposure amount. Exposures should be risk-weighted net of specific provisions (including partial write-offs).

applies_to.note: Core SA arithmetic; binding on all banks applying the standardised approach, which is the only option for most small North American banks.

R-CRE20.1-sa-rwa-net-of-provisions.portfolio_relevance: Sets the multiplicative link between portfolio composition and RWA: shifting balances toward lower-weighted asset classes reduces RWA proportionally, and building specific provisions reduces the exposure base that is risk-weighted.

R-CRE20.2-irb-requires-supervisory-appro.title: IRB approach requires explicit supervisory approval
R-CRE20.2-irb-requires-supervisory-appro.statement: The internal ratings-based approach may only be used with the explicit approval of the bank's supervisor; absent approval a bank must use the standardised approach.
R-CRE20.2-irb-requires-supervisory-appro.quote: The second risk-weighted capital treatment for measuring credit risk, the internal ratings-based (IRB) approach, allows banks to use their internal rating systems for credit risk, subject to the explicit approval of the bank

applies_to.note: Explicit supervisory-approval gate. Small US/Canadian banks are effectively standardised-approach-only, so every CRE20 risk weight binds them directly with no model-based relief.

R-CRE20.2-irb-requires-supervisory-appro.portfolio_relevance: Removes any option for a small bank to lower credit-card RWA through internally estimated PD/LGD; portfolio optimisation must operate purely through the fixed SA weights in this chapter.

R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-at-least-annuall.title: Counterparty due diligence at origination and at least annually
R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-at-least-annuall.statement: Banks must perform due diligence to understand the risk profile and characteristics of their counterparties at origination and on a regular basis at least annually.
R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-at-least-annuall.quote: banks must perform due diligence to ensure that they have an adequate understanding, at origination and thereafter on a regular basis (at least annually), of the risk profile and characteristics of their counterparties.

applies_to.note: Applies to all SA banks; CRE20.4 footnote exempts sovereign, PSE and MDB exposures in CRE20.7 to CRE20.12.

R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-at-least-annuall.portfolio_relevance: Imposes a fixed per-account monitoring cost on any expansion of the counterparty book, which raises the operating cost of growing granular retail/SME lending relative to holding exempt sovereign paper.

R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-proportionality.title: Due diligence sophistication scales with bank size and complexity
R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-proportionality.statement: The sophistication of a bank's credit due diligence should be proportionate to the size and complexity of that bank's activities.
R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-proportionality.quote: The sophistication of the due diligence should be appropriate to the size and complexity of banks

applies_to.note: Explicit proportionality clause: this is the clearest size-sensitivity gate in CRE20 and is what allows a small bank a lighter due-diligence apparatus than a large one.

R-CRE20.4-due-diligence-proportionality.portfolio_relevance: Lets a small bank grow a simple, homogeneous portfolio (eg standardised credit-card lending) without building the analytical infrastructure a complex portfolio would demand.

R-CRE20.7-sovereign-risk-weight-table.title: Risk weights for sovereign and central bank exposures
R-CRE20.7-sovereign-risk-weight-table.statement: Exposures to sovereigns and their central banks are risk-weighted 0%, 20%, 50%, 100% or 150% by external rating band, with 100% for unrated.
R-CRE20.7-sovereign-risk-weight-table.quote: Exposures to sovereigns and their central banks will be risk-weighted as follows: Risk weight table for sovereigns and central banks Table 1 External rating AAA to A+ to Below B– BBB+ to BB+ to B– Unrated AA– A– BBB– Risk weight 0% 20% 50% 100% 150% 100%

applies_to.note: Rating-based table; in jurisdictions that prohibit regulatory use of external ratings (eg the United States under Dodd-Frank s939A) an alternative national treatment applies.

R-CRE20.7-sovereign-risk-weight-table.portfolio_relevance: Makes Treasury/agency and central bank balances the zero-RWA sink: shifting a dollar out of credit cards into domestic sovereign exposure removes essentially all of its capital charge.

R-CRE20.8-domestic-currency-sovereign-di.title: National discretion for lower risk weight on domestic-currency sovereign exposure
R-CRE20.8-domestic-currency-sovereign-di.statement: At national discretion a lower risk weight may be applied to a bank's exposures to its own sovereign or central bank of incorporation when denominated and funded in domestic currency.
R-CRE20.8-domestic-currency-sovereign-di.quote: At national discretion, a lower risk weight may be applied to banks’ exposures to their sovereign (or central bank) of incorporation denominated in domestic currency and funded in that currency.

applies_to.note: National discretion gate; in the US this is exercised as a 0% weight on US Treasury and Federal Reserve exposures.

R-CRE20.8-domestic-currency-sovereign-di.portfolio_relevance: Confirms domestic government securities as the capital-free liquidity buffer a small bank can hold instead of risk-weighted loans.

R-CRE20.10-zero-rw-named-supranationals.title: 0% risk weight for named international organisations
R-CRE20.10-zero-rw-named-supranationals.statement: Exposures to the BIS, IMF, ECB, the European Union, the ESM and the EFSF may receive a 0% risk weight.
R-CRE20.10-zero-rw-named-supranationals.quote: Exposures to the Bank for International Settlements, the International Monetary Fund, the European Central Bank, the European Union, the European Stability Mechanism and the European Financial Stability Facility may receive a 0% risk weight.

applies_to.note: Materially relevant only to banks with international securities portfolios; rarely held by small North American banks.

R-CRE20.10-zero-rw-named-supranationals.portfolio_relevance: Adds a second zero-RWA asset class, but one that small domestic banks generally cannot access, so it is not a practical substitution target for credit-card exposure.

R-CRE20.11-pse-risk-weight-options.title: Risk weights for non-central government public sector entities
R-CRE20.11-pse-risk-weight-options.statement: Exposures to domestic public sector entities are risk-weighted at national discretion under either an option keyed to the sovereign's external rating (20/50/100/100/150/100%) or an option keyed to the PSE's own rating.
R-CRE20.11-pse-risk-weight-options.quote: Exposures to domestic PSEs will be risk-weighted at national discretion, according to either of the following two options. Risk weight table for PSEs Option 1: Based on external rating of sovereign Table 3 External rating of the AAA to A+ to BBB+ to BB+ to Below Unrated sovereign AA– A– BBB– B– B– 20% 50% 100% 100% 150% 100%

applies_to.note: National discretion selects between Option 1 and Option 2; US banks apply a 20% weight to general obligation municipal exposures under 12 CFR 217.

R-CRE20.11-pse-risk-weight-options.portfolio_relevance: Municipal and agency paper sits at 20-50% versus 75-100% for retail loans, so it is a mid-range RWA parking place for a small bank de-risking a card book.

R-CRE20.14-mdb-zero-risk-weight.title: 0% risk weight for eligible multilateral development banks
R-CRE20.14-mdb-zero-risk-weight.statement: Exposures to multilateral development banks that satisfy the Committee's eligibility criteria receive a 0% risk weight, with eligibility assessed case by case.
R-CRE20.14-mdb-zero-risk-weight.quote: A 0% risk weight will be applied to exposures to MDBs that fulfil to the Committee’s satisfaction the eligibility criteria provided below. The Committee will continue to evaluate eligibility on a case-by-case basis.

applies_to.note: Committee-maintained eligibility list; not a practical holding for most small North American banks.

numeric_values: majority of external ratings must be AAA
shareholder ratings of AA- or better
R-CRE20.14-mdb-zero-risk-weight.portfolio_relevance: Another zero-weight substitute for risk-weighted lending, but access is limited in practice to banks with securities-portfolio breadth.

R-CRE20.15-other-mdb-50pct-no-ratings.title: Risk weights for non-eligible MDB exposures, including the no-ratings 50% weight
R-CRE20.15-other-mdb-50pct-no-ratings.statement: Exposures to MDBs not qualifying for 0% are weighted 20% to 150% by external rating, and banks in jurisdictions that do not allow external ratings weight such exposures at 50%.
R-CRE20.15-other-mdb-50pct-no-ratings.quote: Banks incorporated in jurisdictions that do not allow external ratings for regulatory purposes will risk-weight such exposures at 50%. Risk weight table for MDB exposures Table 5 External rating of AAA to A+ to BBB+ to BB+ to Below Unrated counterparty AA– A– BBB– B– B– “Base” risk weight 20% 30% 50% 100% 150% 50%

applies_to.note: The 50% flat weight is the branch that binds US banks, which cannot use external ratings for regulatory purposes.

R-CRE20.15-other-mdb-50pct-no-ratings.portfolio_relevance: Prices non-AAA supranational exposure at 50%, roughly two thirds of the regulatory retail weight, so it is a partial rather than full de-risking substitute.

R-CRE20.16-bank-exposure-definition.title: Definition of a bank exposure
R-CRE20.16-bank-exposure-definition.statement: A bank exposure is a claim, including loans and senior debt instruments, on any financial institution licensed to take deposits from the public and subject to appropriate prudential standards and supervision.
R-CRE20.16-bank-exposure-definition.quote: a bank exposure is defined as a claim (including loans and senior debt instruments, unless considered as subordinated debt for the purposes of CRE20.60) on any financial institution that is licensed to take deposits from the public and is subject to appropriate prudential standards and level of supervision.

applies_to.note: Determines whether interbank placements and correspondent balances get bank weights rather than corporate weights.

R-CRE20.16-bank-exposure-definition.portfolio_relevance: Classifies a small bank's fed funds sold and correspondent balances into the bank exposure class, which carries materially lower weights than its loan book.

R-CRE20.18-bank-ecra-risk-weight-table.title: ECRA base and short-term risk weights for bank exposures
R-CRE20.18-bank-ecra-risk-weight-table.statement: Rated bank exposures receive base risk weights of 20%, 30%, 50%, 100% or 150% by rating band, with short-term exposure weights of 20%, 20%, 20%, 50% and 150%.
R-CRE20.18-bank-ecra-risk-weight-table.quote: Risk weight table for bank exposures External Credit Risk Assessment Approach Table 6 External rating of counterparty AAA to A+ to BBB+ to BB+ to Below AA– A– BBB– B– B– “Base” risk weight 20% 30% 50% 100% 150% Risk weight for short-term 20% 20% 20% 50% 150% exposures

applies_to.note: Applies only in jurisdictions permitting regulatory use of external ratings; not available to US banks, which must use the SCRA in CRE20.21.

R-CRE20.18-bank-ecra-risk-weight-table.portfolio_relevance: Where available, high-grade interbank exposure at 20-30% is a much cheaper use of the balance sheet than 75% regulatory retail lending.

R-CRE20.19-bank-short-term-maturity-wind.title: Maturity windows qualifying for short-term bank risk weights
R-CRE20.19-bank-short-term-maturity-wind.statement: Bank exposures with an original maturity of three months or less, and trade-related bank exposures arising from cross-border movement of goods with an original maturity of six months or less, may use the short-term risk weight column.
R-CRE20.19-bank-short-term-maturity-wind.quote: Exposures to banks with an original maturity of three months or less, as well as exposures to banks that arise from the movement of goods across national borders with an original maturity of six months or less can be assigned a risk weight that correspond to the risk weights for short term exposures in Table 6.

applies_to.note: Applies to the ECRA table; the parallel SCRA maturity rule is CRE20.31.

numeric_values: original maturity of three months or less
original maturity of six months or less
R-CRE20.19-bank-short-term-maturity-wind.portfolio_relevance: Rewards shortening interbank tenor: rolling three-month placements attract a 20% weight where longer tenor could attract 30-50%.

R-CRE20.20-due-diligence-one-bucket-high.title: Due diligence can only ratchet risk weights up, never down
R-CRE20.20-due-diligence-one-bucket-high.statement: If due diligence reveals higher risk than the external rating bucket implies, the bank must assign a risk weight at least one bucket higher, and due diligence may never justify a lower risk weight than the external rating gives.
R-CRE20.20-due-diligence-one-bucket-high.quote: If the due diligence analysis reflects higher risk characteristics than that implied by the external rating bucket of the exposure (ie AAA to AA–; A+ to A– etc), the bank must assign a risk weight at least one bucket higher than the "base" risk weight determined by the external rating. Due diligence analysis must never result in the application of a lower risk weight than that determined by the external rating.

applies_to.note: Asymmetric override; parallel provisions appear at CRE20.39 for covered bonds and CRE20.42 for corporates.

R-CRE20.20-due-diligence-one-bucket-high.portfolio_relevance: Caps any RWA benefit from strong internal credit analysis on rated exposures, so portfolio de-risking must come from asset-class substitution rather than analytical argument.

R-CRE20.21-scra-three-grade-risk-weights.title: SCRA Grade A/B/C risk weights for bank exposures
R-CRE20.21-scra-three-grade-risk-weights.statement: Under the standardised credit risk assessment approach banks classify bank exposures into Grades A, B and C with base risk weights of 40%, 75% and 150% and short-term weights of 20%, 50% and 150%.
R-CRE20.21-scra-three-grade-risk-weights.quote: The SCRA requires banks to classify bank exposures into one of three risk-weight buckets (ie Grades A, B and C) and assign the corresponding risk weights in Table 7. For the purposes of the SCRA only, “published minimum regulatory requirements” in CRE20.22 to excludes liquidity standards. CRE20.30 Risk weight table for bank exposures Standardised Credit Risk Assessment Approach Table 7 Credit risk assessment of Grade B Grade A Grade C counterparty “Base” risk weight 40% 75% 150% Risk weight for short-term 50% 20% 150% exposures

applies_to.note: This is the branch that binds banks in jurisdictions prohibiting regulatory use of external ratings, ie all US banks, and also covers unrated bank exposures everywhere.

R-CRE20.21-scra-three-grade-risk-weights.portfolio_relevance: Fixes the RWA cost of a small bank's correspondent and fed funds book at 40% for sound counterparties, well below the 75% weight on its regulatory retail portfolio.

R-CRE20.21fn-scra-30pct-cet1-14-leverage.title: 30% SCRA weight for very strongly capitalised unrated banks
R-CRE20.21fn-scra-30pct-cet1-14-leverage.statement: Unrated bank exposures may receive a 30% risk weight if the counterparty bank has a CET1 ratio of at least 14% and a Tier 1 leverage ratio of at least 5%, and also meets all Grade A requirements.
R-CRE20.21fn-scra-30pct-cet1-14-leverage.quote: Under the SCRA, exposures to banks without an external credit rating may receive a risk weight of 30%, provided that the counterparty bank has a Common Equity Tier 1 ratio which meets or exceeds 14% and a Tier 1 leverage ratio which meets or exceeds 5%.

applies_to.note: Directly computable from a counterparty's published call report ratios, making it one of the few CRE20 tests a small bank can evaluate from public data.

numeric_values: Tier 1 leverage ratio meets or exceeds 5%
R-CRE20.21fn-scra-30pct-cet1-14-leverage.portfolio_relevance: Creates a measurable incentive to concentrate interbank placements with counterparties whose published CET1 exceeds 14%, cutting that exposure's weight from 40% to 30%.

R-CRE20.29-grade-c-trigger-12-months.title: Mandatory Grade C classification triggers
R-CRE20.29-grade-c-trigger-12-months.statement: A bank exposure must be classified as Grade C if the counterparty fails the Grade B published-minimum-requirements test, or if within the previous 12 months an auditor issued an adverse opinion or expressed substantial going-concern doubt.
R-CRE20.29-grade-c-trigger-12-months.quote: At a minimum, if any of the following triggers is breached, a bank must classify the exposure into Grade C: (1) The counterparty bank does not meet the criteria for being classified as Grade B with respect to its published minimum regulatory requirements, as set out in CRE20.25 and; or CRE20.26 (2) Where audited financial statements are required, the external auditor has issued an adverse audit opinion or has expressed substantial doubt about the counterparty bank’s ability to continue as a going concern in its financial statements or audited reports within the previous 12 months.

applies_to.note: Objective, publicly observable triggers keyed to audited financial statements.

R-CRE20.29-grade-c-trigger-12-months.portfolio_relevance: A counterparty downgrade to Grade C nearly quadruples that exposure's weight from 40% to 150%, so concentration in weakly capitalised correspondents is a latent RWA cliff.

R-CRE20.32-scra-sovereign-floor.title: Sovereign risk weight floor on foreign-currency bank exposures
R-CRE20.32-scra-sovereign-floor.statement: Under the SCRA a floor equal to the risk weight of the sovereign of the counterparty bank's country of incorporation applies to bank exposures that are not denominated in the relevant local currency.
R-CRE20.32-scra-sovereign-floor.quote: To reflect transfer and convertibility risk under the SCRA, a risk-weight floor based on the risk weight applicable to exposures to the sovereign of the country where the bank counterparty is incorporated will be applied to the risk weight assigned to bank exposures.

applies_to.note: Bites only where a bank holds cross-border, non-local-currency interbank exposure.

R-CRE20.32-scra-sovereign-floor.portfolio_relevance: Penalises cross-border interbank diversification for a bank whose alternative is domestic lending, since the sovereign floor can dominate the counterparty's own grade.

R-CRE20.34-covered-bond-cover-pool-limit.title: Eligible cover pool composition limits for covered bonds
R-CRE20.34-covered-bond-cover-pool-limit.statement: To qualify for covered bond risk weights the cover pool must consist of eligible claims including residential real estate claims with LTV of 80% or lower and commercial real estate claims with LTV of 60% or lower, with claims on banks weighted 30% or lower limited to 15% of covered bond issuances.
R-CRE20.34-covered-bond-cover-pool-limit.quote: In order to be eligible for the risk weights set out in CRE20.38, the underlying assets (the cover pool) of covered bonds as defined in CRE20.33 shall meet the requirements set out in CRE20.37 and shall include any of the following: (1) claims on, or guaranteed by, sovereigns, their central banks, public sector entities or multilateral development banks; (2) claims secured by residential real estate that meet the criteria set out in CRE20.71 and with a loan-to-value ratio of 80% or lower; (3) claims secured by commercial real estate that meets the criteria set out in CRE20.71 and with a loan-to-value ratio of 60% or lower; or (4) claims on, or guaranteed by banks that qualify for a 30% or lower risk weight. However, such assets cannot exceed 15% of covered bond issuances.

applies_to.note: Covered bonds are essentially absent from small North American bank balance sheets.

numeric_values: cannot exceed 15% of covered bond issuances
R-CRE20.34-covered-bond-cover-pool-limit.portfolio_relevance: Defines an alternative low-weight mortgage-backed holding, but one that is not a realistic substitution target for a small US bank shrinking a card book.

R-CRE20.35-covered-bond-10pct-overcollat.title: 10% minimum overcollateralisation of covered bond cover pools
R-CRE20.35-covered-bond-10pct-overcollat.statement: The nominal value of the cover pool assigned to a covered bond should exceed the bond's nominal outstanding value by at least 10%, and where the legislative framework does not require this the issuer must publicly disclose that the 10% is met in practice.
R-CRE20.35-covered-bond-10pct-overcollat.quote: The nominal value of the pool of assets assigned to the covered bond instrument (s) by its issuer should exceed its nominal outstanding value by at least 10%.

applies_to.note: Combines a quantitative pool test with a public disclosure obligation on the issuing bank.

R-CRE20.35-covered-bond-10pct-overcollat.portfolio_relevance: Sets the economic cost of issuing covered bonds as a funding tool: 110 units of eligible assets must be encumbered per 100 units raised.

R-CRE20.37-covered-bond-disclosure-90dpd.title: Covered bond investor information: 90-day arrears, at least semi-annually
R-CRE20.37-covered-bond-disclosure-90dpd.statement: A bank investing in covered bonds must receive portfolio information including the percentage of loans more than 90 days past due, made available by the issuer at least semi-annually, to use the covered bond risk weights.
R-CRE20.37-covered-bond-disclosure-90dpd.quote: the percentage of loans more than 90 days past due; and (2) the issuer makes the information referred to in point (1) available to the bank at least semi-annually.

applies_to.note: Information-availability condition on the investing bank; failure loses the preferential weights.

R-CRE20.37-covered-bond-disclosure-90dpd.portfolio_relevance: Makes the low covered-bond weight contingent on an ongoing data feed, an operational burden that discourages small banks from using this asset class.

R-CRE20.38-covered-bond-risk-weight-tabl.title: Risk weights for rated and unrated covered bonds
R-CRE20.38-covered-bond-risk-weight-tabl.statement: Rated covered bonds receive base risk weights of 10%, 20%, 20%, 50% or 100% by issue-specific rating; unrated covered bonds are inferred from the issuing bank's risk weight, giving 10%, 15%, 20%, 25%, 35%, 50% or 100%.
R-CRE20.38-covered-bond-risk-weight-tabl.quote: Risk weight table for rated covered bond exposures Table 8 Issue-specific rating of the AAA to A+ to BBB+ to BB+ to Below covered bond AA– A– BBB– B– B– “Base” risk weight 10% 20% 20% 50% 100% Risk weight table for unrated covered bond exposures Table 9 Risk weight of the 30% 20% 40% 50% 75% 100% 150% issuing bank “Base” risk weight 10% 15% 20% 25% 35% 50% 100%

applies_to.note: Unrated table is the operative one where external ratings cannot be used for regulatory purposes.

R-CRE20.38-covered-bond-risk-weight-tabl.portfolio_relevance: Covered bonds at 10-25% are among the cheapest credit assets available, so any shift from card lending into them cuts RWA by roughly 70-85% per dollar.

R-CRE20.40-securities-firms-treated-as-b.title: Classification of securities firms and other financial institutions
R-CRE20.40-securities-firms-treated-as-b.statement: Exposures to securities firms and other financial institutions are treated as bank exposures only if those firms are subject to prudential standards and supervision equivalent to banks; all others are treated as corporate exposures.
R-CRE20.40-securities-firms-treated-as-b.quote: Exposures to securities firms and other financial institutions will be treated as exposures to banks provided that these firms are subject to prudential standards and a level of supervision equivalent to those applied to banks (including capital and liquidity requirements). National supervisors should determine whether the regulatory and supervisory framework governing securities firms and other financial institutions in their own jurisdictions is equivalent to that which is applied to banks in their own jurisdictions. Where the regulatory and supervisory framework governing securities firms and other financial institutions is determined to be equivalent to that applied to banks in a jurisdiction, other national supervisors may allow their banks to risk weight such exposures to securities firms and other financial institutions as exposures to banks. Exposures to all other securities firms and financial institutions will be treated as exposures to corporates.

applies_to.note: National supervisors determine equivalence, so this is a national-discretion classification gate.

R-CRE20.40-securities-firms-treated-as-b.portfolio_relevance: Determines whether exposure to non-bank lenders and fintech partners is weighted as bank (40%) or corporate (100%), a 60 percentage point swing that matters for card programmes run through non-bank partners.

R-CRE20.41-corporate-exposure-definition.title: Definition of the corporate exposure class
R-CRE20.41-corporate-exposure-definition.statement: Corporate exposures comprise claims on incorporated entities, associations, partnerships, proprietorships, trusts, funds and similar entities that do not qualify for another exposure class, and expressly exclude exposures to individuals.
R-CRE20.41-corporate-exposure-definition.quote: exposures to corporates include exposures (loans, bonds, receivables, etc) to incorporated entities, associations, partnerships, proprietorships, trusts, funds and other entities with similar characteristics, except those which qualify for one of the other exposure classes. The treatment associated with subordinated debt and equities of these counterparties is addressed in CRE20.53 to CRE20.62. The corporate exposure class includes exposures to insurance companies and other financial corporates that do not meet the definitions of exposures to banks, or securities firms and other financial institutions, as determined in CRE20.16 and CRE20.40 respectively. The corporate exposure class does not include exposures to individuals.

applies_to.note: Residual class: anything not fitting sovereign, PSE, MDB, bank, retail or real estate falls here.

R-CRE20.41-corporate-exposure-definition.portfolio_relevance: Because it excludes individuals, this definition is what forces consumer card balances into the retail class and its 45/75/100% weights rather than the 100% corporate weight.

R-CRE20.42-corporate-ecra-due-diligence.title: Corporate base risk weights from external ratings, subject to due diligence
R-CRE20.42-corporate-ecra-due-diligence.statement: Banks in jurisdictions allowing regulatory use of external ratings assign corporate base risk weights from Table 10 and must perform due diligence to confirm those ratings conservatively reflect counterparty creditworthiness.
R-CRE20.42-corporate-ecra-due-diligence.quote: For corporate exposures of banks incorporated in jurisdictions that allow the use of external ratings for regulatory purposes, banks will assign "base" risk weights according to Table 10.

applies_to.note: Not operative in the United States, where external ratings may not be used for regulatory capital purposes.

R-CRE20.42-corporate-ecra-due-diligence.portfolio_relevance: Where available, investment-grade corporate lending at 20-50% is materially cheaper in RWA terms than retail lending at 75%.

R-CRE20.43-unrated-corporate-100pct.title: 100% risk weight for unrated corporates and the rated corporate table
R-CRE20.43-unrated-corporate-100pct.statement: Unrated corporate exposures receive a 100% risk weight except for unrated corporate SMEs, and rated corporate exposures are weighted 20%, 75%, 50%, 100% or 150% by rating band.
R-CRE20.43-unrated-corporate-100pct.quote: Unrated corporate exposures of banks incorporated in jurisdictions that allow the use of external ratings for regulatory purposes will receive a 100% risk weight, with the exception of unrated exposures to corporate small or medium-sized entities (SMEs), as described in CRE20.47. Risk weight table for corporate exposures Jurisdictions that use external ratings for regulatory purposes Table 10 External rating of AAA to A+ to BBB+ to BB+ to Below Unrated counterparty AA– A– BBB– BB– BB– “Base” risk weight 20% 75% 50% 100% 150% 100%

applies_to.note: The unrated 100% weight is the practical default for the vast majority of a small bank's commercial borrowers.

R-CRE20.43-unrated-corporate-100pct.portfolio_relevance: Sets 100% as the baseline cost of commercial lending, meaning a shift from unrated corporate loans into regulatory retail at 75% actually lowers RWA per dollar.

R-CRE20.44-corporate-100pct-no-external-.title: Flat 100% corporate risk weight where external ratings are not permitted
R-CRE20.44-corporate-100pct-no-external-.statement: In jurisdictions that do not allow regulatory use of external ratings, all corporate exposures receive a 100% risk weight except investment grade corporates under CRE20.46 and corporate SMEs under CRE20.47.
