R-RBC20.6-credit-rwa-sa-or-irb.title: Credit RWA for banking book exposures uses the standardised or IRB approach
R-RBC20.6-credit-rwa-sa-or-irb.statement: Credit RWA for banking book exposures must be calculated using either the standardised approach in CRE20 to CRE22 or the internal ratings-based approach in CRE30 to CRE36.
R-RBC20.6-credit-rwa-sa-or-irb.quote: (1) Credit RWA for banking book exposures, except the RWA listed in (2) to (6) below, calculated using: (a) The standardised approach, set out in CRE20 to; or CRE22 (b) The internal ratings-based (IRB) approach, set out in CRE30 to CRE36.

applies_to.note: IRB requires supervisory approval; small banks are effectively confined to the standardised approach.

R-RBC20.6-credit-rwa-sa-or-irb.portfolio_relevance: Fixes which risk-weight schedule a credit card book is measured under, and therefore whether portfolio composition changes translate into RWA through fixed standardised weights or through modelled PD/LGD/EAD.

R-RBC20.6-sec-1250-fallback.title: 1250% risk weight fallback for securitisation exposures
R-RBC20.6-sec-1250-fallback.statement: Where a bank cannot use SEC-SA, SEC-ERBA, IAA or SEC-IRBA for a banking book securitisation exposure, a risk weight of 1250% applies.
R-RBC20.6-sec-1250-fallback.quote: (e) A risk weight of 1250% in cases where the bank cannot use (a) to (d) above.

applies_to.note: Applies to banking book securitisation exposures under CRE40 to CRE45.

R-RBC20.6-sec-1250-fallback.portfolio_relevance: A 1250% weight is capital-for-dollar equivalent to full deduction at the 8% minimum, so retained tranches of a credit card master trust that fail the approach hierarchy are effectively deducted and make securitising the card book capital-inefficient.

R-RBC20.10-oprisk-sa-only.title: Operational risk RWA uses only the standardised approach
R-RBC20.10-oprisk-sa-only.statement: RWA for operational risk must be calculated using the standardised approach for operational risk in OPE25.
R-RBC20.10-oprisk-sa-only.quote: RWA for operational risk is calculated using the standardised approach for operational risk, set out in OPE25.

applies_to.note: No internally modelled option remains for operational risk.

R-RBC20.10-oprisk-sa-only.portfolio_relevance: Because the standardised operational risk measure scales with income, a card portfolio's high fee and interest income mechanically adds operational RWA to the same denominator that its credit RWA sits in.

R-RBC20.11-floor-base-sa-credit.title: Base of the output floor uses the standardised approach for credit risk
R-RBC20.11-floor-base-sa-credit.statement: The base of the output floor must be calculated using the standardised approach for credit risk and the other listed standardised approaches.
R-RBC20.11-floor-base-sa-credit.quote: The standardised approaches to be used to calculate the base of the output floor referenced in RBC20.4 (2) are as follows: (1) The standardised approach for credit risk.

applies_to.note: Only relevant to banks with nominated modelled approaches.

R-RBC20.11-floor-base-sa-credit.portfolio_relevance: Forces even an IRB card lender to run the CRE20 standardised retail risk weights in parallel, so standardised transactor/revolver weights remain the reference point for portfolio decisions.

R-RBC20.12-irb-excluded-from-floor.title: IRB and internal models may not be used in the output floor base
R-RBC20.12-irb-excluded-from-floor.statement: The IRB approach to credit risk, SEC-IRBA, the market risk IMA, the VaR models approach and IMM must not be used, directly or by cross reference, in calculating the base of the output floor.
R-RBC20.12-irb-excluded-from-floor.quote: the following approaches are not permitted to be used, directly or by cross reference, in the calculation of the base of the output floor: (1) IRB approach to credit risk;

applies_to.note: Definitional consequence of RBC20.11.

R-RBC20.12-irb-excluded-from-floor.portfolio_relevance: Removes any possibility of using modelled credit card parameters to lower the floor, so the floor benchmark for a card book is always the standardised risk weight.

R-RBC20.14-sa-only-jurisdiction-complian.title: A jurisdiction implementing only standardised approaches is compliant
R-RBC20.14-sa-only-jurisdiction-complian.statement: A jurisdiction that does not implement some or all internally modelled approaches, and instead implements only the basic or standardised approaches, is compliant with the Basel framework.
R-RBC20.14-sa-only-jurisdiction-complian.quote: a jurisdiction which does not implement some or all of the internally modelled approaches but instead only implements the basic or standardised approaches is compliant with the Basel framework.

applies_to.note: National discretion; explains why small North American banks are evaluated only against standardised outcomes.

R-RBC20.14-sa-only-jurisdiction-complian.portfolio_relevance: Justifies evaluating a small bank's credit card portfolio purely against standardised risk weights, since no modelled relief is available to it in practice.

R-RBC30.2-conservation-buffer-2.5-cet1.title: Capital conservation buffer of 2.5% must be met with CET1
R-RBC30.2-conservation-buffer-2.5-cet1.statement: A capital conservation buffer of 2.5% of RWA, comprised of Common Equity Tier 1, is established above the regulatory minimum capital requirement, and capital distribution constraints apply when capital falls into that range.
R-RBC30.2-conservation-buffer-2.5-cet1.quote: A capital conservation buffer of 2.5%, comprised of Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1), is established above the regulatory minimum capital requirement. Capital distribution constraints will be imposed on a bank when capital levels fall within this range.

applies_to.note: Applied at the consolidated level; national supervisors may also apply it at solo level.

R-RBC30.2-conservation-buffer-2.5-cet1.portfolio_relevance: Adds 2.5 percentage points of CET1 on top of every dollar of credit card RWA before a bank can distribute freely, making RWA-light portfolio mixes directly worth more dividend capacity.

R-RBC30.2-cet1-priority-to-minimums.title: CET1 counts toward the buffer only after the minimums are met
R-RBC30.2-cet1-priority-to-minimums.statement: Common Equity Tier 1 must first be used to meet the minimum capital and TLAC requirements, including the 6% Tier 1 and 8% Total capital requirements, before the remainder can contribute to the capital conservation buffer.
R-RBC30.2-cet1-priority-to-minimums.quote: Common Equity Tier 1 must first be used to meet the minimum capital and total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) requirements if necessary (including the 6% Tier 1, 8% Total capital requirements), before the remainder can contribute to the capital conservation buffer.

applies_to.note: TLAC element only binds G-SIB resolution entities; the 6%/8% element binds all banks.

R-RBC30.2-cet1-priority-to-minimums.portfolio_relevance: A bank with little AT1 or Tier 2 must plug the Tier 1 and Total capital shortfalls with CET1 first, so the buffer that protects its credit card dividend capacity is smaller than the headline CET1 ratio suggests.

R-RBC30.4-conservation-ratio-table.title: Minimum capital conservation ratios by CET1 band
R-RBC30.4-conservation-ratio-table.statement: A bank with a CET1 ratio of 4.5%-5.125% must conserve 100% of earnings; above 5.125% to 5.75%, 80%; above 5.75% to 6.375%, 60%; above 6.375% to 7.0%, 40%; and above 7.0%, none.
R-RBC30.4-conservation-ratio-table.quote: Individual bank minimum capital conservation standards CET1 Ratio Minimum Capital Conservation Ratios (expressed as a percentage of earnings) 4.5% - 5.125% 100% >5.125% - 5.75% 80% >5.75% - 6.375% 60% >6.375% - 7.0% 40% > 7.0% 0%

applies_to.note: Bands widen when the buffer is extended by the countercyclical buffer or a systemic surcharge (RBC30.17, RBC30.18).

R-RBC30.4-conservation-ratio-table.portfolio_relevance: This is the step function that converts an RWA increase from credit card growth directly into a dividend payout cap, so a portfolio shift that pushes CET1 across a 0.625pp band boundary costs 20 percentage points of payout capacity.

R-RBC30.4-recalculate-each-distribution.title: Conservation standards recalculated at each distribution date
R-RBC30.4-recalculate-each-distribution.statement: The applicable capital conservation standards must be recalculated at each distribution date.
R-RBC30.4-recalculate-each-distribution.quote: The applicable conservation standards must be recalculated at each distribution date.

applies_to.note: Determines the observation frequency for a compliance test against quarterly filings.

R-RBC30.4-recalculate-each-distribution.portfolio_relevance: Makes the constraint a point-in-time quarterly test, so seasonal credit card balance build-ups that inflate RWA at a quarter-end can trigger a payout restriction on that date.

R-RBC30.4-80pct-conservation-example.title: Worked example: 80% earnings conservation in the second buffer quartile
R-RBC30.4-80pct-conservation-example.statement: A bank with a CET1 ratio between 5.125% and 5.75% must conserve 80% of its earnings in the subsequent payment period, paying out no more than 20% in dividends, share buybacks and discretionary bonus payments.
R-RBC30.4-80pct-conservation-example.quote: a bank with a CET1 capital ratio in the range of 5.125% to 5.75% is required to conserve 80% of its earnings in the subsequent payment period (ie pay out no more than 20% in terms of dividends, share buybacks and discretionary bonus payments)

applies_to.note: Illustrative example that fixes the meaning of 'conserve' as a cap on the payout ratio.

R-RBC30.4-80pct-conservation-example.portfolio_relevance: Defines the payout cap as a share of earnings rather than a level, so a card book whose earnings fall in a downturn also loses distribution capacity in absolute terms just as loss rates peak.

R-RBC30.4-cet1-ratio-measurement.title: CET1 used for the buffer test excludes CET1 needed for Tier 1 and Total capital minimums
R-RBC30.4-cet1-ratio-measurement.statement: The CET1 ratio used for the conservation test includes amounts meeting the 4.5% CET1 minimum but excludes CET1 needed to meet the 6% Tier 1 and 8% Total Capital requirements.
R-RBC30.4-cet1-ratio-measurement.quote: The CET1 ratio includes amounts used to meet the 4.5% minimum CET1 requirement, but excludes any additional CET1 needed to meet the 6% Tier 1 and 8% Total Capital requirements

applies_to.note: Critical measurement convention for computing the buffer from published ratios.

R-RBC30.4-cet1-ratio-measurement.portfolio_relevance: For a small bank with no AT1 or Tier 2, the usable buffer is the reported CET1 ratio minus 8%, not minus 4.5%, which materially tightens the RWA budget available for credit card growth.

R-RBC30.4-raise-capital-to-distribute.title: Private capital raising as an alternative to conserving earnings
R-RBC30.4-raise-capital-to-distribute.statement: A bank wishing to distribute more than the constraint permits may raise capital in the private sector equal to the amount above the constraint it wishes to distribute.
R-RBC30.4-raise-capital-to-distribute.quote: If the bank wants to make payments in excess of the constraints imposed by this regime, it would have the option of raising capital in the private sector equal to the amount above the constraint which it wishes to distribute.

applies_to.note: To be discussed with the supervisor as part of the capital planning process.

R-RBC30.4-raise-capital-to-distribute.portfolio_relevance: Gives a lever other than shrinking the credit portfolio: equity issuance can substitute for RWA reduction when the buffer is eroded by card loss provisions.

R-RBC30.5-definition-of-distributions.title: Definition of items subject to the distribution restriction
R-RBC30.5-definition-of-distributions.statement: Distributions subject to the restriction include dividends, share buybacks, discretionary payments on other Tier 1 capital instruments and discretionary bonus payments to staff.
R-RBC30.5-definition-of-distributions.quote: Items considered to be distributions include dividends and share buybacks, discretionary payments on other Tier 1 capital instruments and discretionary bonus payments to staff.

applies_to.note: Payments that do not deplete CET1, such as certain scrip dividends, are excluded.

R-RBC30.5-definition-of-distributions.portfolio_relevance: Because AT1 coupons are inside the restricted set, a bank that funded card growth with AT1 rather than CET1 finds those coupons cut off at exactly the moment the card book is generating losses.

R-RBC30.5-declared-dividend-exemption.title: Already-declared and removed dividends are exempt from the restriction
R-RBC30.5-declared-dividend-exemption.statement: Distribution restrictions do not apply to dividends that cannot legally be cancelled, have already been removed from CET1, and were declared in line with the applicable conservation standards at the time of declaration.
R-RBC30.5-declared-dividend-exemption.quote: The distribution restrictions do not apply to dividends which satisfy all three of the following conditions: (a) the dividends cannot legally be cancelled by the bank; (b) the dividends have already been removed from CET1; and (c) the dividends were declared in line with the applicable capital conservation standards (as set out in RBC30.4) at the time of declaration.

applies_to.note: All three conditions must be satisfied.

R-RBC30.5-declared-dividend-exemption.portfolio_relevance: Creates a timing carve-out: dividends declared before a credit card loss event erodes the buffer remain payable, so the constraint bites with a one-period lag on the observed payout series.

R-RBC30.5-definition-of-earnings.title: Definition of earnings for the conservation calculation
R-RBC30.5-definition-of-earnings.statement: Earnings are distributable profits calculated prior to the deduction of elements subject to the restriction on distributions, and calculated after the tax that would have been reported had none of the distributable items been paid.
R-RBC30.5-definition-of-earnings.quote: Earnings are defined as distributable profits calculated prior to the deduction of elements subject to the restriction on distributions. Earnings are calculated after the tax which would have been reported had none of the distributable items been paid.

applies_to.note: Tax effects of distributions are reversed out.

R-RBC30.5-definition-of-earnings.portfolio_relevance: Sets the base against which the conservation percentage bites; provisions on a credit card book reduce distributable profits and therefore reduce the absolute permitted distribution twice over.

R-RBC30.5-no-positive-earnings-below-7.title: No positive net distributions where earnings are negative and CET1 is below 7%
R-RBC30.5-no-positive-earnings-below-7.statement: Where a bank does not have positive earnings and has a CET1 ratio below 7% (or higher if the buffer has been expanded), it is restricted from making positive net distributions.
R-RBC30.5-no-positive-earnings-below-7.quote: Where a bank does not have positive earnings and has a CET1 ratio less than 7% (or higher if the capital conservation buffer has been expanded by other buffers), it would be restricted from making positive net distributions.

applies_to.note: The 7% threshold rises when the countercyclical buffer or a systemic surcharge extends the conservation buffer.

R-RBC30.5-no-positive-earnings-below-7.portfolio_relevance: A single loss-making quarter driven by credit card charge-offs, combined with a CET1 ratio under 7%, produces an absolute dividend ban rather than a proportional cut.

R-RBC30.5-consolidated-application.title: Buffer regime applied at the consolidated level
R-RBC30.5-consolidated-application.statement: The capital conservation framework should be applied at the consolidated level, with national supervisors having the option to apply it at solo level.
R-RBC30.5-consolidated-application.quote: The framework should be applied at the consolidated level, ie restrictions would be imposed on distributions out of the consolidated group. National supervisors would have the option of applying the regime at the solo level to conserve resources in specific parts of the group.

applies_to.note: National discretion to impose the regime at solo level.

R-RBC30.5-consolidated-application.portfolio_relevance: Fixes the reporting entity for the test as the consolidated holding company, matching the level at which a small US bank publishes its card portfolio and capital ratios.

R-RBC30.5-supervisory-time-limits.title: Supervisors may impose time limits on operating in the buffer range
R-RBC30.5-supervisory-time-limits.statement: Supervisors have additional discretion to impose time limits on banks operating within the buffer range on a case-by-case basis, and should ensure capital plans rebuild buffers over an appropriate timeframe.
R-RBC30.5-supervisory-time-limits.quote: supervisors have the additional discretion to impose time limits on banks operating within the buffer range on a case-by-case basis.

applies_to.note: Explicit case-by-case supervisory discretion.

R-RBC30.5-supervisory-time-limits.portfolio_relevance: Means a bank cannot indefinitely run a high-RWA credit card strategy inside the buffer range; a supervisory deadline can force RWA reduction on a fixed timetable.

R-RBC30.9-ccyb-range-0-2.5.title: National countercyclical buffer varies between zero and 2.5% of RWA
R-RBC30.9-ccyb-range-0-2.5.statement: A national countercyclical capital buffer requirement will vary between zero and 2.5% of risk-weighted assets depending on the authority's judgement of system-wide risk.
R-RBC30.9-ccyb-range-0-2.5.quote: This will vary between zero and 2.5% of risk weighted assets, depending on their judgement as to the extent of the build up of system-wide risk.

applies_to.note: Set by the designated national authority; deployment is expected to be infrequent.

R-RBC30.9-ccyb-range-0-2.5.portfolio_relevance: Adds up to 2.5 further percentage points of CET1 per dollar of credit card RWA in a credit boom, which is precisely when card balances and RWA are growing fastest.

R-RBC30.9-reciprocity-cap-2.5.title: Mandatory reciprocity capped at a 2.5% countercyclical buffer
R-RBC30.9-reciprocity-cap-2.5.statement: National authorities may set a buffer above 2.5% for their own banks, but the international reciprocity provisions treat the maximum countercyclical buffer as 2.5%.
R-RBC30.9-reciprocity-cap-2.5.quote: the international reciprocity provisions set out in this regime treat the maximum countercyclical buffer as 2.5%.

applies_to.note: National authorities may implement a buffer in excess of 2.5% domestically.

R-RBC30.9-reciprocity-cap-2.5.portfolio_relevance: Caps the imported buffer cost of cross-border private sector credit exposures at 2.5%, bounding the buffer penalty from a geographically diversified card book.

R-RBC30.11-preannouncement-12-months.title: Twelve-month pre-announcement for increases, immediate effect for decreases
R-RBC30.11-preannouncement-12-months.statement: A jurisdiction will pre-announce a decision to raise the countercyclical buffer by up to 12 months, while decisions to decrease it take effect immediately.
R-RBC30.11-preannouncement-12-months.quote: To give banks time to adjust to a buffer level, a jurisdiction will pre-announce its decision to raise the level of the countercyclical buffer by up to 12 months. Decisions by a jurisdiction to decrease the level of the countercyclical buffer will take effect immediately.

applies_to.note: Where a jurisdiction's pre-announcement period is shorter, home authorities should match it subject to a maximum of 12 months.

R-RBC30.11-preannouncement-12-months.portfolio_relevance: Gives a bank a four-quarter window to re-price or run off credit card balances before an increased buffer bites, and lets it re-lever immediately on release.

R-RBC30.12-bank-specific-ccyb-cet1.title: Bank-specific countercyclical buffer must be met with CET1
R-RBC30.12-bank-specific-ccyb-cet1.statement: Banks are subject to a countercyclical buffer varying between zero and 2.5% of total RWA, reflecting the geographic composition of their credit exposures, and must meet it with CET1 or face restrictions on distributions.
R-RBC30.12-bank-specific-ccyb-cet1.quote: Banks will be subject to a countercyclical buffer that varies between zero and 2.5% to total risk weighted assets. The buffer that will apply to each bank will reflect the geographic composition of its portfolio of credit exposures. Banks must meet this buffer with CET1 or be subject to the restrictions on distributions set out in RBC30.17.

applies_to.note: Applied at the consolidated level; national supervisors may apply it at solo level.

R-RBC30.12-bank-specific-ccyb-cet1.portfolio_relevance: Only CET1 counts, so a bank cannot use AT1 or Tier 2 to absorb a countercyclical add-on on a growing credit card book; the buffer must come from retained earnings or common equity.

R-RBC30.13-private-sector-credit-exposur.title: Definition of private sector credit exposures for the countercyclical buffer
R-RBC30.13-private-sector-credit-exposur.statement: Private sector credit exposures for the countercyclical buffer weighting include all private sector credit exposures attracting a credit risk capital charge, plus risk weighted equivalent trading book charges for specific risk, the incremental risk charge and securitisation.
R-RBC30.13-private-sector-credit-exposur.quote: Credit exposures in this case include all private sector credit exposures that attract a credit risk capital charge or the risk weighted equivalent trading book capital charges for specific risk, the incremental risk charge and securitisation.

applies_to.note: Stated for internationally active banks, but the definition is what determines the weight for any bank subject to the buffer.

R-RBC30.13-private-sector-credit-exposur.portfolio_relevance: Credit card receivables are squarely private sector credit exposures, so they carry full weight in determining the bank-specific countercyclical add-on.

R-RBC30.13-interbank-sovereign-excluded.title: Interbank and public sector exposures excluded from the buffer weighting
R-RBC30.13-interbank-sovereign-excluded.statement: Interbank exposures and exposures to the public sector are excluded from private sector credit exposures, but non-bank financial sector exposures are included.
R-RBC30.13-interbank-sovereign-excluded.quote: Interbank exposures and exposures to the public sector are excluded, but non-bank financial sector exposures are included.

applies_to.note: FAQ interpretation of RBC30.13.

R-RBC30.13-interbank-sovereign-excluded.portfolio_relevance: Shifting a balance sheet from credit cards into sovereign or interbank assets removes that exposure from the countercyclical buffer weighting entirely, on top of the risk-weight saving.

R-RBC30.14-ccyb-weighting-formula.title: Countercyclical buffer weights are credit risk charge shares by jurisdiction
R-RBC30.14-ccyb-weighting-formula.statement: The weight applied to each jurisdiction's buffer is the bank's total credit risk charge relating to private sector credit exposures in that jurisdiction divided by its total credit risk charge relating to private sector credit exposures across all jurisdictions.
R-RBC30.14-ccyb-weighting-formula.quote: The weighting applied to the buffer in place in each jurisdiction will be the bank’s total credit risk charge that relates to private sector credit exposures in that jurisdiction, divided by the bank’s total credit risk charge that relates to private sector credit exposures across all jurisdictions.

applies_to.note: Banks should use an ultimate risk basis where possible; a purely domestic small bank has a weight of 1 on its home jurisdiction.

numeric_values: weight = jurisdictional credit risk charge / total credit risk charge
R-RBC30.14-ccyb-weighting-formula.portfolio_relevance: Weights are charge-based not balance-based, so a high-risk-weight product like credit cards pulls the bank-specific buffer rate more strongly toward its jurisdiction's rate than an equally sized mortgage book would.

R-RBC30.16-ccyb-extends-conservation-buf.title: Countercyclical buffer implemented as an extension of the conservation buffer
R-RBC30.16-ccyb-extends-conservation-buf.statement: The countercyclical buffer requirement is implemented through an extension of the capital conservation buffer.
R-RBC30.16-ccyb-extends-conservation-buf.quote: The countercyclical buffer requirement to which a bank is subject is implemented through an extension of the capital conservation buffer described in RBC30.1 to RBC30.5.

applies_to.note: Mechanically means the same distribution constraint machinery applies.

R-RBC30.16-ccyb-extends-conservation-buf.portfolio_relevance: Confirms the buffers stack into a single distribution test, so credit card RWA growth erodes conservation and countercyclical headroom simultaneously.

R-RBC30.17-quartile-conservation-table.title: Conservation ratios by quartile of the extended buffer
R-RBC30.17-quartile-conservation-table.statement: When the buffer is extended, a bank in the first quartile of the buffer must conserve 100% of earnings, second quartile 80%, third quartile 60%, fourth quartile 40%, and above the top of the buffer 0%.
R-RBC30.17-quartile-conservation-table.quote: Individual bank minimum capital conservation standards Common Equity Tier 1 (including other fully Minimum Capital Conservation Ratios loss absorbing capital) (expressed as a percentage of earnings) Within first quartile of buffer 100% Within second quartile of buffer 80% Within Third quartile of buffer 60% Within Fourth quartile of buffer 40% Above top of buffer 0%

applies_to.note: The buffer is always divided into four equal bands regardless of its total width.

R-RBC30.17-quartile-conservation-table.portfolio_relevance: Generalises the payout step function to any buffer width, so the RWA reduction needed to move up one payout band scales with the total buffer requirement.

R-RBC30.18-ccyb-2.5-illustrative-bands.title: Illustrative conservation bands under a 2.5% countercyclical requirement
R-RBC30.18-ccyb-2.5-illustrative-bands.statement: With a 2.5% countercyclical requirement, a bank must conserve 100% of earnings at CET1 of 4.5%-5.75%, 80% above 5.75% to 7.0%, 60% above 7.0% to 8.25%, 40% above 8.25% to 9.5%, and nothing above 9.5%.
R-RBC30.18-ccyb-2.5-illustrative-bands.quote: Individual bank minimum capital conservation standards, when a bank is subject to a 2.5% countercyclical requirement Common Equity Tier 1 Ratio (including Minimum Capital Conservation Ratios other fully loss absorbing capital) (expressed as a percentage of earnings) 4.5% - 5.75% 100% >5.75% - 7.0% 80% >7.0% - 8.25% 60% >8.25% - 9.5% 40% > 9.5% 0%

applies_to.note: Illustrative table; band width is 1.25pp when the total buffer is 5.0%.

R-RBC30.18-ccyb-2.5-illustrative-bands.portfolio_relevance: Shows that at maximum countercyclical settings a bank needs 9.5% CET1 for unrestricted distributions, which is roughly a 2.1x multiple of the bare minimum RWA budget for the same card book.

R-RBC30.19-ccyb-calculation-frequency.title: Countercyclical buffer must be calculated and disclosed at minimum-capital frequency
R-RBC30.19-ccyb-calculation-frequency.statement: Banks must calculate and publicly disclose their countercyclical buffer requirements at least as frequently as their minimum capital requirements, based on the latest available jurisdictional buffer rates.
R-RBC30.19-ccyb-calculation-frequency.quote: Banks must ensure that their countercyclical buffer requirements are calculated and publically disclosed with at least the same frequency as their minimum capital requirements.

applies_to.note: Ties buffer disclosure to the quarterly regulatory reporting cycle.

R-RBC30.19-ccyb-calculation-frequency.portfolio_relevance: Guarantees the buffer rate is observable at the same quarterly frequency as the credit card balances it is applied to, making the constraint testable from public filings.

R-RBC30.20-hold-buffers-above-minimum.title: Banks should hold buffers above the regulatory minimum outside stress
R-RBC30.20-hold-buffers-above-minimum.statement: Outside of periods of stress, banks should hold buffers of capital above the regulatory minimum.
R-RBC30.20-hold-buffers-above-minimum.quote: Outside of periods of stress, banks should hold buffers of capital above the regulatory minimum.

applies_to.note: Expectation rather than a hard ratio.

R-RBC30.20-hold-buffers-above-minimum.portfolio_relevance: Establishes that a bank running its credit card book at the bare regulatory minimum in benign conditions is already non-compliant with supervisory expectations.

R-RBC30.22-retention-increases-near-mini.title: Earnings retention should increase the closer capital is to the minimum
R-RBC30.22-retention-increases-near-mini.statement: Absent private capital raising, the share of earnings retained to rebuild capital buffers should increase the nearer a bank's actual capital levels are to the minimum capital requirement.
R-RBC30.22-retention-increases-near-mini.quote: in the absence of raising capital in the private sector, the share of earnings retained by banks for the purpose of rebuilding their capital buffers should increase the nearer their actual capital levels are to the minimum capital requirement.

applies_to.note: Behavioural principle underpinning the RBC30.4 step function.

R-RBC30.22-retention-increases-near-mini.portfolio_relevance: Establishes the monotone relationship the payout table encodes: as card losses push CET1 down, retention must rise, so the internal capital generation available to fund new card lending falls.

R-RBC30.21-rebuild-by-cutting-distributi.title: Rebuilding depleted buffers by reducing discretionary distributions
R-RBC30.21-rebuild-by-cutting-distributi.statement: When buffers have been drawn down, banks should look to rebuild them by reducing discretionary distributions of earnings, including dividends, buybacks and staff bonus payments, or by raising new private capital.
R-RBC30.21-rebuild-by-cutting-distributi.quote: When buffers have been drawn down, one way banks should look to rebuild them is through reducing discretionary distributions of earnings. This could include reducing dividend payments, share-backs and staff bonus payments.

applies_to.note: The balance between retention and issuance should be discussed with supervisors.

R-RBC30.21-rebuild-by-cutting-distributi.portfolio_relevance: Frames buffer restoration as a numerator action first, which is the alternative a model should compare against the denominator action of shrinking the credit card book.

R-RBC40.1-gsib-hla-cet1-only.title: G-SIB higher loss absorbency must be met with CET1 only
R-RBC40.1-gsib-hla-cet1-only.statement: Global systemically important banks must meet their higher loss absorbency requirement with Common Equity Tier 1 capital only.
R-RBC40.1-gsib-hla-cet1-only.quote: global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) must meet their higher loss absorbency requirement with Common Equity Tier 1 capital only.

applies_to.note: Applies only to banks designated as G-SIBs under SCO40; no small North American bank is in scope.

R-RBC40.1-gsib-hla-cet1-only.portfolio_relevance: Size gate: confirms that the systemic surcharge does not enter the capital budget of a small card lender, so its buffer stack is conservation plus countercyclical only.

R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-calibration.title: G-SIB designation cutoff and higher loss absorbency calibration
R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-calibration.statement: The G-SIB designation cutoff score is 130 bps and buckets span 100 bps each, with the highest populated bucket carrying 2.5% of RWA, an initially empty 3.5% top bucket and 1.0% for the lowest bucket.
R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-calibration.quote: The cutoff score for G- SIB designation is 130 bps and the buckets corresponding to the different higher loss-absorbency requirements each have a range of 100 bps.

applies_to.note: Score-based designation under SCO40.19 to SCO40.22.

R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-calibration.portfolio_relevance: Defines the size/complexity threshold below which no surcharge applies, which is the primary bank-size discriminator in the buffer stack.

R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-table.title: G-SIB higher loss absorbency requirements by bucket
R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-table.statement: Higher loss absorbency requirements by G-SIB bucket are 3.5% for scores 530-629, 2.5% for 430-529, 2.0% for 330-429, 1.5% for 230-329 and 1.0% for 130-229, expressed as common equity as a percentage of RWA.
R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-table.quote: Bucketing approach Table 1 Bucket Score range Higher loss absorbency requirement (common equity as a percentage of risk-weighted assets) 5 530-629 3.5% 4 430-529 2.5% 3 330-429 2.0% 2 230-329 1.5% 1 130-229 1.0%

applies_to.note: G-SIBs only; new buckets increment in 1% steps under RBC40.5.

R-RBC40.4-gsib-bucket-table.portfolio_relevance: For a large card issuer, moving up one systemic bucket adds 0.5pp of CET1 across the whole balance sheet, which can outweigh the return on an incremental card portfolio acquisition.

R-RBC40.6-12-month-bucket-migration.title: Twelve months to meet an increased G-SIB surcharge
R-RBC40.6-12-month-bucket-migration.statement: A G-SIB that progresses to a higher bucket must meet the additional requirement within 12 months, after which the expanded conservation buffer retention mechanism applies.
R-RBC40.6-12-month-bucket-migration.quote: If a G-SIB progresses to a bucket requiring a higher loss absorbency requirement, it will be required to meet the additional requirement within a time frame of 12 months.

applies_to.note: National authorities may require a delay in releasing a reduced requirement.

R-RBC40.6-12-month-bucket-migration.portfolio_relevance: Gives a four-quarter adjustment window in which a large issuer can shrink or securitise a card book rather than raise CET1 against the higher surcharge.

R-RBC40.3-gsib-remediation-plan.title: Capital remediation plan on breach of the G-SIB surcharge
R-RBC40.3-gsib-remediation-plan.statement: A G-SIB that breaches its higher loss absorbency requirement must agree a capital remediation plan and, until compliance is restored, is subject to the dividend payout limitations of the conservation buffer bands.
R-RBC40.3-gsib-remediation-plan.quote: If a G-SIB breaches the higher loss absorbency requirement, it is required to agree a capital remediation plan to return to compliance over a time frame to be established by the supervisor.

applies_to.note: Timeframe is set by the supervisor case by case.

R-RBC40.3-gsib-remediation-plan.portfolio_relevance: Converts a surcharge breach into a supervisor-negotiated deleveraging plan, in which credit card RWA is a natural first target because of its high risk weight per dollar of assets.

R-RBC40.8-dsib-hla-cet1.title: D-SIB higher loss absorbency must be met fully by CET1
R-RBC40.8-dsib-hla-cet1.statement: The higher loss absorbency requirement imposed on a domestic systemically important bank should be met fully by Common Equity Tier 1.
R-RBC40.8-dsib-hla-cet1.quote: The higher loss absorbency requirement should be met fully by Common Equity Tier 1.

applies_to.note: National authorities calibrate D-SIB requirements with substantial discretion; small banks are generally out of scope.

R-RBC40.8-dsib-hla-cet1.portfolio_relevance: A mid-sized North American bank designated a D-SIB must fund any surcharge on its card RWA entirely with common equity, with no AT1 or Tier 2 substitution.

R-RBC40.19-no-double-counting-gsib-dsib.title: G-SIB and D-SIB surcharges are not additive
R-RBC40.19-no-double-counting-gsib-dsib.statement: Higher loss absorbency requirements derived from the G-SIB and D-SIB frameworks should not be additive; double-counting should be avoided.
R-RBC40.19-no-double-counting-gsib-dsib.quote: The higher loss absorbency requirements derived from the G-SIB and D-SIB frameworks should not be additive.

applies_to.note: Home authorities impose the higher of the two, per RBC40.8(3).

R-RBC40.19-no-double-counting-gsib-dsib.portfolio_relevance: Caps the systemic component of the buffer stack at the higher of the two surcharges, bounding the total CET1 hurdle applied to a large issuer's card RWA.

R-RBC40.23-dsib-four-band-extension.title: D-SIB surcharge implemented as a four-band extension of the conservation buffer
R-RBC40.23-dsib-four-band-extension.statement: National authorities should implement the D-SIB higher loss absorbency requirement through an extension of the capital conservation buffer, maintaining the division of the buffer into four bands of equal size.
R-RBC40.23-dsib-four-band-extension.quote: National authorities should implement the higher loss absorbency requirement through an extension of the capital conservation buffer, maintaining the division of the buffer into four bands of equal size (as described in RBC30.17).

applies_to.note: D-SIB designation and calibration are national discretion.

R-RBC40.23-dsib-four-band-extension.portfolio_relevance: Keeps the payout mechanics identical across buffer types, so a single quartile computation on the total buffer suffices to test distribution capacity against a credit card RWA path.

R-CAP10.1-three-capital-categories.title: Regulatory capital consists of three categories
R-CAP10.1-three-capital-categories.statement: Regulatory capital consists of Common Equity Tier 1 and Additional Tier 1 (going-concern capital) and Tier 2 (gone-concern capital), each governed by its own inclusion criteria.
R-CAP10.1-three-capital-categories.quote: Regulatory capital consists of three categories, each governed by a single set of criteria that instruments are required to meet before inclusion in the relevant category. (1) Common Equity Tier 1 (going-concern capital) (2) Additional Tier 1 (going-concern capital) (3) Tier 2 Capital (gone-concern capital)

applies_to.note: Foundational taxonomy for the ratio numerators.

R-CAP10.1-three-capital-categories.portfolio_relevance: Defines the three distinct capital pools whose relative cost determines how expensive an extra unit of credit card RWA is to fund.

R-CAP10.2-total-and-tier1-definition.title: Definition of Total regulatory capital and Tier 1 capital
R-CAP10.2-total-and-tier1-definition.statement: Total regulatory capital is the sum of CET1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 net of CAP30 regulatory adjustments, and Tier 1 capital is the sum of CET1 and Additional Tier 1 net of those adjustments.
R-CAP10.2-total-and-tier1-definition.quote: Total regulatory capital is the sum of Common Equity Tier 1, Additional Tier 1 and Tier 2 capital, net of regulatory adjustments described in CAP30. Tier 1 capital is the sum of Common Equity Tier 1 and Additional Tier 1 capital, net of the regulatory adjustments in CAP30 applied to those categories.

applies_to.note: Supplies the exact numerator construction for the RBC20.1 ratios.

R-CAP10.2-total-and-tier1-definition.portfolio_relevance: Gives the arithmetic that maps a bank's published capital components onto the three ratio numerators against which credit card RWA is tested.

R-CAP10.3-predominant-form-common-shares.title: Predominant form of Tier 1 must be common shares and retained earnings
R-CAP10.3-predominant-form-common-shares.statement: The predominant form of Tier 1 capital must be common shares and retained earnings.
R-CAP10.3-predominant-form-common-shares.quote: the predominant form of Tier 1 capital must be common shares and retained earnings.

applies_to.note: Qualitative composition requirement enforced through the 4.5% CET1 / 6% Tier 1 split.

R-CAP10.3-predominant-form-common-shares.portfolio_relevance: Blocks a strategy of funding credit card RWA growth predominantly through hybrid instruments; retained earnings from the card book must carry most of the load.

R-CAP10.6-cet1-components.title: Components of Common Equity Tier 1
R-CAP10.6-cet1-components.statement: CET1 consists of qualifying common shares, stock surplus on those shares, retained earnings, accumulated other comprehensive income and other disclosed reserves, qualifying minority interest, and the regulatory adjustments applied in the CET1 calculation.
R-CAP10.6-cet1-components.quote: Common Equity Tier 1 capital consists of the sum of the following elements: (1) Common shares issued by the bank that meet the criteria for classification as common shares for regulatory purposes (or the equivalent for non-joint stock companies); (2) Stock surplus (share premium) resulting from the issue of instruments included Common Equity Tier 1; (3) Retained earnings; (4) Accumulated other comprehensive income and other disclosed reserves;

applies_to.note: Minority interest is subject to the separate limits in CAP10.20 to CAP10.26.

R-CAP10.6-cet1-components.portfolio_relevance: Identifies retained earnings and AOCI as the CET1 lines that move with credit card profitability and with unrealised losses on the securities book funding it.

R-CAP10.7-interim-profit-and-dividends.title: Interim profit or loss is included and dividends removed from CET1
R-CAP10.7-interim-profit-and-dividends.statement: Retained earnings and other comprehensive income include interim profit or loss, and dividends are removed from Common Equity Tier 1 in accordance with applicable accounting standards.
R-CAP10.7-interim-profit-and-dividends.quote: Retained earnings and other comprehensive income include interim profit or loss. National authorities may consider appropriate audit, verification or review procedures. Dividends are removed from Common Equity Tier 1 in accordance with applicable accounting standards.

applies_to.note: National authorities may impose audit or review procedures on interim profits.

R-CAP10.7-interim-profit-and-dividends.portfolio_relevance: Means a quarter of elevated credit card provisions flows immediately into CET1 through interim loss recognition, without waiting for year-end audit.

R-CAP10.5-non-cash-dividend-approval.title: Prior supervisory approval for instruments with non-cash, non-share dividends
R-CAP10.5-non-cash-dividend-approval.statement: A bank must seek prior supervisory approval if it intends to include in capital an instrument whose dividends are paid in anything other than cash or shares.
R-CAP10.5-non-cash-dividend-approval.quote: A bank must seek prior supervisory approval if it intends to include in capital an instrument which has its dividends paid in anything other than cash or shares.

applies_to.note: Explicit prior supervisory approval gate.

R-CAP10.5-non-cash-dividend-approval.portfolio_relevance: Adds an approval gate to novel capital structures a bank might use to fund credit expansion, slowing the numerator-side response to RWA growth.

R-CAP10.11-at1-call-after-five-years.title: Additional Tier 1 instruments callable only after five years and with approval
R-CAP10.11-at1-call-after-five-years.statement: An Additional Tier 1 instrument may be callable at the initiative of the issuer only after a minimum of five years, and the bank must receive prior supervisory approval to exercise a call.
R-CAP10.11-at1-call-after-five-years.quote: (5) May be callable at the initiative of the issuer only after a minimum of five years: (a) To exercise a call option a bank must receive prior supervisory approval;

applies_to.note: Tax and regulatory event calls are permitted earlier only with supervisory agreement.

R-CAP10.11-at1-call-after-five-years.portfolio_relevance: Locks AT1 funding in for at least five years, so a bank that issues AT1 to support card growth cannot cheaply unwind the capital when the portfolio shrinks.

R-CAP10.11-at1-5.125-trigger.title: Additional Tier 1 loss absorption trigger of at least 5.125% CET1
R-CAP10.11-at1-5.125-trigger.statement: Additional Tier 1 instruments classified as liabilities must convert to common shares or be written down at an objective pre-specified trigger point of at least 5.125% Common Equity Tier 1.
R-CAP10.11-at1-5.125-trigger.quote: (a) conversion to common shares at an objective pre-specified trigger point of at least 5.125% Common Equity Tier 1; or (b) a writedown mechanism which allocates losses to the instrument at a pre-specified trigger point of at least 5.125% Common Equity Tier 1.

applies_to.note: Applies to instruments classified as liabilities for accounting purposes.

R-CAP10.11-at1-5.125-trigger.portfolio_relevance: Places a contractual conversion point 0.625pp above the 4.5% CET1 minimum, giving a hard CET1 floor that credit card loss scenarios must be stress-tested against.

R-CAP10.11-at1-full-payment-discretion.title: Additional Tier 1 requires full discretion to cancel distributions
R-CAP10.11-at1-full-payment-discretion.statement: For an instrument to count as Additional Tier 1, the bank must have full discretion at all times to cancel distributions or payments, and such cancellation must not be an event of default.
R-CAP10.11-at1-full-payment-discretion.quote: (a) the bank must have full discretion at all times to cancel distributions /payments (b) cancellation of discretionary payments must not be an event of default

applies_to.note: Dividend pushers are prohibited; cancelled payments must be fully available to the bank.

R-CAP10.11-at1-full-payment-discretion.portfolio_relevance: Makes AT1 coupons cancellable exactly when the buffer distribution constraint bites, so AT1 raised against card RWA behaves as loss-absorbing rather than fixed funding cost.

R-CAP10.16-tier2-five-year-amortisation.title: Tier 2 minimum five-year maturity with straight-line amortisation
R-CAP10.16-tier2-five-year-amortisation.statement: A Tier 2 instrument must have a minimum original maturity of at least five years and its recognition in regulatory capital in the final five years before maturity is amortised on a straight line basis.
R-CAP10.16-tier2-five-year-amortisation.quote: (4) Maturity: (a) Minimum original maturity of at least five years (b) Recognition in regulatory capital in the remaining five years before maturity will be amortised on a straight line basis.

applies_to.note: No step-ups or other incentives to redeem are permitted.

numeric_values: 20% per year straight-line amortisation in final 5 years
R-CAP10.16-tier2-five-year-amortisation.portfolio_relevance: Tier 2 capital supporting a credit card book decays 20% a year in the final five years, so a bank relying on subordinated debt must refinance or shrink RWA on a predictable schedule.

R-CAP10.18-general-provisions-1.25-cap.title: General provisions in Tier 2 capped at 1.25% of standardised credit RWA
R-CAP10.18-general-provisions-1.25-cap.statement: Under the standardised approach, general provisions and general loan-loss reserves eligible for inclusion in Tier 2, measured gross of tax effects, are limited to a maximum of 1.25 percentage points of credit risk-weighted assets calculated under the standardised approach.
R-CAP10.18-general-provisions-1.25-cap.quote: general provisions/general loan-loss reserves eligible for inclusion in Tier 2, measured gross of tax effects, will be limited to a maximum of 1.25 percentage points of credit risk-weighted assets (RWA) calculated under the standardised approach.

applies_to.note: Standardised approach only; CCP RWA is included in the calculation base but CVA RWA is not.

numeric_values: 1.25 percentage points of standardised credit RWA
R-CAP10.18-general-provisions-1.25-cap.portfolio_relevance: Directly relevant to card lenders: a credit card portfolio typically carries an allowance far above 1.25% of RWA, so the excess allowance gives no Tier 2 credit and provisioning becomes a pure drag on CET1.

R-CAP10.18-specific-provisions-excluded.title: Provisions against identified deterioration are excluded from Tier 2
R-CAP10.18-specific-provisions-excluded.statement: Provisions ascribed to identified deterioration of particular assets or known liabilities, whether individual or grouped, must be excluded from the loan-loss reserves eligible for Tier 2.
R-CAP10.18-specific-provisions-excluded.quote: Provisions ascribed to identified deterioration of particular assets or known liabilities, whether individual or grouped, should be excluded.

applies_to.note: Distinguishes general from specific provisions under the standardised approach.

R-CAP10.18-specific-provisions-excluded.portfolio_relevance: Under lifetime expected-loss accounting most of a card allowance relates to identified deterioration, so very little of the allowance can be recycled into Tier 2 as the book seasons.

R-CAP10.19-irb-excess-provisions-0.6-cap.title: IRB excess provisions recognised in Tier 2 up to 0.6% of IRB credit RWA
R-CAP10.19-irb-excess-provisions-0.6-cap.statement: Under the IRB approach, where total eligible provisions exceed the total expected loss amount, banks may recognise the difference in Tier 2 capital up to a maximum of 0.6% of credit risk-weighted assets calculated under the IRB approach, and a lower national limit may apply.
R-CAP10.19-irb-excess-provisions-0.6-cap.quote: banks may recognise the difference in Tier 2 capital up to a maximum of 0.6% of credit risk-weighted assets calculated under the internal ratings-based approach. At national discretion, a limit lower than 0.6% may be applied.

applies_to.note: Explicit national discretion to apply a limit below 0.6%; requires IRB approval.

R-CAP10.19-irb-excess-provisions-0.6-cap.portfolio_relevance: For an IRB card lender, over-provisioning the card book buys back Tier 2 capital only up to 0.6% of IRB credit RWA, a much tighter cap than the 1.25% available under the standardised approach.

R-CAP10.20-minority-interest-eligibility.title: Minority interest recognised in CET1 only if issued by a bank subsidiary
R-CAP10.20-minority-interest-eligibility.statement: Minority interest from common shares issued by a fully consolidated subsidiary may be recognised in CET1 only if the instrument would meet the common share criteria if issued by the bank and the issuing subsidiary is itself a bank.
R-CAP10.20-minority-interest-eligibility.quote: Minority interest arising from the issue of common shares by a fully consolidated subsidiary of the bank may receive recognition in Common Equity Tier 1 only if: (1) the instrument giving rise to the minority interest would, if issued by the bank, meet all of the criteria for classification as common shares for regulatory capital purposes; and (2) the subsidiary that issued the instrument is itself a bank.

applies_to.note: Any institution subject to the same minimum prudential standards and supervision as a bank may be treated as a bank; minority interest is excluded entirely where the parent funds it.

R-CAP10.20-minority-interest-eligibility.portfolio_relevance: Prevents a group from creating CET1 capacity for a card-issuing non-bank subsidiary by selling minority stakes in it.

R-CAP10.21-minority-surplus-7.0-threshol.title: Minority interest surplus measured against 7.0% CET1 including the buffer
R-CAP10.21-minority-surplus-7.0-threshol.statement: Surplus CET1 of a subsidiary, which is excluded from consolidated CET1 in proportion to minority ownership, is measured against the lower of the subsidiary's minimum CET1 requirement plus the capital conservation buffer (7.0% of RWA) and the subsidiary's share of the consolidated requirement.
R-CAP10.21-minority-surplus-7.0-threshol.quote: (a) the minimum Common Equity Tier 1 requirement of the subsidiary plus the capital conservation buffer (ie 7.0% of consolidated RWA); and

applies_to.note: Requires the subsidiary's requirement to be computed on a sub-consolidated basis even if it is not separately regulated.

R-CAP10.21-minority-surplus-7.0-threshol.portfolio_relevance: Anchors the effective CET1 requirement at 7.0% (4.5% + 2.5%) even inside the definition of capital, confirming 7% as the practical CET1 budget for credit RWA.

R-CAP10.23-tier1-surplus-8.5-threshold.title: Tier 1 surplus of subsidiaries measured against 8.5% of RWA
R-CAP10.23-tier1-surplus-8.5-threshold.statement: Surplus Tier 1 of a subsidiary is measured against the lower of the subsidiary's minimum Tier 1 requirement plus the capital conservation buffer (8.5% of RWA) and its share of the consolidated requirement.
R-CAP10.23-tier1-surplus-8.5-threshold.quote: (a) the minimum Tier 1 requirement of the subsidiary plus the capital conservation buffer (ie 8.5% of RWA); and

applies_to.note: Relevant only to groups with partly owned consolidated bank subsidiaries.

R-CAP10.23-tier1-surplus-8.5-threshold.portfolio_relevance: Fixes 8.5% as the fully-buffered Tier 1 target, which combined with the 7.0% CET1 target defines the AT1 capacity available to support credit RWA.

R-CAP10.25-total-capital-surplus-10.5-th.title: Total capital surplus of subsidiaries measured against 10.5% of RWA
R-CAP10.25-total-capital-surplus-10.5-th.statement: Surplus Total Capital of a subsidiary is measured against the lower of the subsidiary's minimum Total Capital requirement plus the capital conservation buffer (10.5% of RWA) and its share of the consolidated requirement.
R-CAP10.25-total-capital-surplus-10.5-th.quote: (a) the minimum Total Capital requirement of the subsidiary plus the capital conservation buffer (ie 10.5% of RWA); and

applies_to.note: Relevant only to groups with partly owned consolidated subsidiaries issuing capital to third parties.

R-CAP10.25-total-capital-surplus-10.5-th.portfolio_relevance: Establishes 10.5% as the fully-buffered Total capital target, the outer boundary of the capital budget a credit portfolio must fit inside.

R-CAP10.26-spv-capital-not-cet1.title: Capital issued to third parties out of an SPV cannot be CET1
R-CAP10.26-spv-capital-not-cet1.statement: Where capital has been issued to third parties out of a special purpose vehicle, none of it may be included in Common Equity Tier 1, though it may qualify for consolidated Additional Tier 1 or Tier 2 if the strict conditions are met.
R-CAP10.26-spv-capital-not-cet1.quote: Where capital has been issued to third parties out of an SPV, none of this capital can be included in Common Equity Tier 1.

applies_to.note: Applies to all SPVs irrespective of accounting consolidation; the SPV's only asset must be its investment in the bank's capital.

R-CAP10.26-spv-capital-not-cet1.portfolio_relevance: Blocks the use of a card securitisation vehicle or similar SPV to manufacture CET1, forcing the highest-quality capital supporting a card book to be issued directly.

R-CAP30.7-goodwill-intangibles-deduction.title: Goodwill and other intangibles deducted from CET1
R-CAP30.7-goodwill-intangibles-deduction.statement: Goodwill and all other intangibles must be deducted in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1, net of any associated deferred tax liability that would be extinguished on impairment, with mortgage servicing rights treated under the threshold deductions.
R-CAP30.7-goodwill-intangibles-deduction.quote: Goodwill and all other intangibles must be deducted in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1

applies_to.note: Includes goodwill embedded in significant investments in unconsolidated financial entities; right-of-use lease assets over tangible underlyings are not deducted.

R-CAP30.7-goodwill-intangibles-deduction.portfolio_relevance: Acquiring a credit card portfolio at a premium creates goodwill that is deducted dollar-for-dollar from CET1 while the acquired receivables still add RWA, making portfolio purchases far more capital-intensive than organic origination.

R-CAP30.9-dta-future-profitability-deduc.title: Deferred tax assets relying on future profitability deducted from CET1
R-CAP30.9-dta-future-profitability-deduc.statement: DTAs that rely on future profitability of the bank to be realised must be deducted from CET1; those relating to temporary differences are subject to the threshold deduction, while operating-loss DTAs are deducted in full net of eligible DTLs.
R-CAP30.9-dta-future-profitability-deduc.quote: Deferred tax assets (DTAs) that rely on future profitability of the bank to be realised are to be deducted in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1.

applies_to.note: DTAs may be netted with DTLs only where the same taxation authority levies both and offsetting is permitted.

R-CAP30.9-dta-future-profitability-deduc.portfolio_relevance: Credit card allowances generate temporary-difference DTAs, so heavy provisioning cuts CET1 twice: once through the loss and again through the deduction of the resulting DTA above the threshold.

R-CAP30.9-operating-loss-dta-no-threshol.title: Operating-loss DTAs deducted in full without threshold benefit
R-CAP30.9-operating-loss-dta-no-threshol.statement: DTAs arising from net operating losses must be deducted from Common Equity Tier 1 in full and do not benefit from the 10% threshold.
R-CAP30.9-operating-loss-dta-no-threshol.quote: All DTAs that depend on the future profitability of the bank to be realised and that arise from net operating losses are required to be deducted from Common Equity Tier 1 in full and so do not benefit from the 10% threshold.

applies_to.note: The one-year realisability test used in some jurisdictions is not applicable under Basel III.

R-CAP30.9-operating-loss-dta-no-threshol.portfolio_relevance: A loss year in a monoline-style card book converts into operating-loss DTAs that are fully deducted, so CET1 falls by more than the accounting loss just as RWA needs support.

R-CAP30.11-cash-flow-hedge-reserve.title: Cash flow hedge reserve derecognised in CET1
R-CAP30.11-cash-flow-hedge-reserve.statement: The portion of the cash flow hedge reserve relating to hedges of items not fair valued on the balance sheet must be derecognised in the calculation of CET1, with positive amounts deducted and negative amounts added back.
R-CAP30.11-cash-flow-hedge-reserve.quote: The amount of the cash flow hedge reserve that relates to the hedging of items that are not fair valued on the balance sheet (including projected cash flows) should be derecognised in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1.

applies_to.note: Removes artificial volatility where only one leg of the hedge is fair valued.

R-CAP30.11-cash-flow-hedge-reserve.portfolio_relevance: Neutralises the CET1 effect of hedging the funding cost of a floating-rate card book, so hedging decisions do not distort the measured capital budget.

R-CAP30.13-el-provision-shortfall-deduct.title: Shortfall of provisions to expected losses deducted from CET1
R-CAP30.13-el-provision-shortfall-deduct.statement: IRB banks must compare total eligible provisions with the total expected loss amount, and where expected loss exceeds eligible provisions the difference must be deducted from Common Equity Tier 1, with no reduction for tax effects.
R-CAP30.13-el-provision-shortfall-deduct.quote: Where the total expected loss amount exceeds total eligible provisions, banks must deduct the difference from Common Equity Tier 1. The full amount is to be deducted and should not be reduced by any tax effects that could be expected to occur if provisions were to rise to the level of expected losses.

applies_to.note: IRB approach only; securitisation exposures are excluded from both sides of the comparison.

R-CAP30.13-el-provision-shortfall-deduct.portfolio_relevance: For an IRB card lender, the high expected loss of a revolving retail book must be matched by provisions or the gap is a direct CET1 deduction, making under-provisioned card growth immediately capital-destructive.

R-CAP30.14-securitisation-gain-on-sale-d.title: Securitisation gain on sale deducted from CET1
R-CAP30.14-securitisation-gain-on-sale-d.statement: Banks must deduct from Common Equity Tier 1 any increase in equity capital resulting from a securitisation transaction, such as that associated with expected future margin income resulting in a gain on sale recognised in regulatory capital.
R-CAP30.14-securitisation-gain-on-sale-d.quote: Banks must deduct from Common Equity Tier 1 any increase in equity capital resulting from a securitisation transaction, such as that associated with expected future margin income resulting in a gain on sale that is recognised in regulatory capital.

applies_to.note: Applies irrespective of the approach used for the underlying exposures.

R-CAP30.14-securitisation-gain-on-sale-d.portfolio_relevance: Directly limits the classic credit card securitisation play: a bank cannot boost CET1 by capitalising excess spread on a securitised card book, so securitisation only helps through RWA relief, not through gain recognition.

R-CAP30.15-own-credit-risk-derecognition.title: Own credit risk gains and losses derecognised in CET1
R-CAP30.15-own-credit-risk-derecognition.statement: All unrealised gains and losses resulting from changes in the fair value of liabilities due to changes in the bank's own credit risk must be derecognised in the calculation of CET1, including derivative valuation adjustments, with no offsetting against counterparty credit valuation adjustments.
R-CAP30.15-own-credit-risk-derecognition.quote: Derecognise in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1, all unrealised gains and losses that have resulted from changes in the fair value of liabilities that are due to changes in the bank’s own credit risk.

applies_to.note: Offsetting between own-credit and counterparty-credit valuation adjustments is not allowed.

R-CAP30.15-own-credit-risk-derecognition.portfolio_relevance: Stops a bank whose credit spread widens because of card portfolio deterioration from booking an offsetting CET1 gain on its own fair-valued liabilities.

R-CAP30.16-pension-asset-deduction.title: Defined benefit pension fund net assets deducted from CET1
R-CAP30.16-pension-asset-deduction.statement: Defined benefit pension fund liabilities must be fully recognised in CET1, and each net pension asset on the balance sheet must be deducted from CET1 net of any associated deferred tax liability; assets to which the bank has unrestricted access can offset the deduction with supervisory approval.
R-CAP30.16-pension-asset-deduction.quote: For each defined benefit pension fund that is an asset on the balance sheet, the net asset on the balance sheet in respect of the plan or fund should be deducted in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1

applies_to.note: Offsetting requires supervisory approval and unrestricted, unfettered access to the fund assets.

R-CAP30.16-pension-asset-deduction.portfolio_relevance: Removes pension surplus from the capital available to support credit RWA, which for an older small bank can be a material reduction in the credit growth budget.

R-CAP30.18-own-shares-deduction.title: Investments in own common shares deducted from CET1
R-CAP30.18-own-shares-deduction.statement: All of a bank's investments in its own common shares, whether held directly or indirectly, and any own stock the bank could be contractually obliged to purchase, must be deducted in the calculation of CET1 irrespective of banking or trading book location.
R-CAP30.18-own-shares-deduction.quote: All of a bank’s investments in its own common shares, whether held directly or indirectly, will be deducted in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1

applies_to.note: Gross long positions may be netted against short positions only where the short involves no counterparty risk; index holdings must be looked through.

R-CAP30.18-own-shares-deduction.portfolio_relevance: Makes buybacks and forward purchase commitments an immediate CET1 cost, so a bank shrinking its card book to fund a buyback gets no capital relief from the treasury shares.

R-CAP30.21-reciprocal-cross-holdings-ful.title: Reciprocal cross-holdings of capital deducted in full
R-CAP30.21-reciprocal-cross-holdings-ful.statement: Reciprocal cross-holdings of capital designed to artificially inflate the capital position of banks must be deducted in full using a corresponding deduction approach, applied to the same component of capital for which the instrument would qualify if issued by the bank itself.
R-CAP30.21-reciprocal-cross-holdings-ful.quote: Reciprocal cross-holdings of capital that are designed to artificially inflate the capital position of banks will be deducted in full.

applies_to.note: Applies to holdings in other banks, other financial institutions and insurance entities; guarantees count as capital up to the maximum payable.

R-CAP30.21-reciprocal-cross-holdings-ful.portfolio_relevance: Prevents a network of small banks from mutually funding each other's capital to expand credit card lending capacity beyond genuine third-party equity.

R-CAP30.22-underwriting-five-working-day.title: Underwriting positions held five working days or less may be excluded
R-CAP30.22-underwriting-five-working-day.statement: Underwriting positions in capital instruments or other TLAC liabilities held for five working days or less can be excluded from the investment calculation, while those held longer must be included.
R-CAP30.22-underwriting-five-working-day.quote: (4) Underwriting positions in capital instruments or other TLAC liabilities held for five working days or less can be excluded. Underwriting positions held for longer than five working days must be included.

applies_to.note: Relevant to banks with underwriting operations; rarely material for small deposit-funded banks.

R-CAP30.22-underwriting-five-working-day.portfolio_relevance: Gives a short, hard-edged holding window for underwritten financial-sector paper before it starts consuming the same CET1 that supports the credit portfolio.

R-CAP30.25-non-gsib-tlac-5pct-threshold.title: Non-G-SIB holdings of other TLAC liabilities below 5% of common equity
R-CAP30.25-non-gsib-tlac-5pct-threshold.statement: A bank that is not a G-SIB must deduct holdings of other TLAC liabilities from Tier 2 unless such holdings are, in aggregate and on a gross long basis, less than 5% of the bank's common equity, or fall within the 10% threshold.
R-CAP30.25-non-gsib-tlac-5pct-threshold.quote: If a bank is not a G-SIB, its holdings of other TLAC liabilities must be deducted from Tier 2 capital resources, unless: (1) such holdings are, in aggregate and on a gross long basis, less than 5% of the bank’s common equity (after applying all other regulatory adjustments listed in full prior to CAP30.22); or (2) the holdings fall within the 10% threshold provided in CAP30.26.

applies_to.note: Explicitly the non-G-SIB branch of the TLAC holdings rule; measured after all prior regulatory adjustments.

R-CAP30.25-non-gsib-tlac-5pct-threshold.portfolio_relevance: Caps how much G-SIB TLAC paper a small bank can hold as a liquidity asset before it starts eating Tier 2, which competes with the Tier 2 headroom supporting its credit book.

R-CAP30.26-10pct-threshold-deduction.title: Non-significant financial holdings above 10% of common equity deducted
R-CAP30.26-10pct-threshold-deduction.statement: Where holdings of capital instruments and other TLAC liabilities in unconsolidated financial entities exceed, in aggregate and on a net long basis, 10% of the bank's common equity, the amount above 10% must be deducted using a corresponding deduction approach.
R-CAP30.26-10pct-threshold-deduction.quote: in aggregate and on a net long basis exceed 10% of the bank’s common equity (after applying all other regulatory adjustments in full listed prior to CAP30.22) then the amount above 10% is required to be deducted.

applies_to.note: Deduction is split across CET1, AT1 and Tier 2 in proportion to the composition of the holdings.

R-CAP30.26-10pct-threshold-deduction.portfolio_relevance: Puts a hard 10% ceiling on financial-sector equity exposures before they consume capital, steering a small bank's balance sheet toward lending assets such as cards rather than financial-institution securities.

R-CAP30.27-shortfall-next-higher-tier.title: Deduction shortfall cascades to the next higher tier of capital
R-CAP30.27-shortfall-next-higher-tier.statement: If a bank is required to make a deduction from a particular tier of capital and does not have enough of that tier, the shortfall must be deducted from the next higher tier of capital.
R-CAP30.27-shortfall-next-higher-tier.quote: If a bank is required to make a deduction from a particular tier of capital and it does not have enough of that tier of capital to satisfy that deduction, the shortfall will be deducted from the next higher tier of capital

applies_to.note: Particularly relevant to banks with no AT1 or Tier 2 outstanding, where all deductions land on CET1.

R-CAP30.27-shortfall-next-higher-tier.portfolio_relevance: A small bank with no AT1 or Tier 2 absorbs every deduction directly in CET1, so its credit RWA budget is more sensitive to deductions than a larger bank with a full capital stack.

R-CAP30.28-non-deducted-amounts-risk-wei.title: Amounts not deducted continue to be risk weighted
R-CAP30.28-non-deducted-amounts-risk-wei.statement: Amounts not deducted continue to be risk weighted, with banking book instruments treated under the IRB or standardised approach as applicable, and holdings allocated pro rata between amounts below and above the threshold.
R-CAP30.28-non-deducted-amounts-risk-wei.quote: Amounts that are not deducted will continue to be risk weighted. Thus, instruments in the trading book will be treated as per the market risk rules and instruments in the banking book should be treated as per the IRB approach or the standardised approach (as applicable).

applies_to.note: Deducted amounts may be excluded from RWA; amounts below the threshold must be included.

R-CAP30.28-non-deducted-amounts-risk-wei.portfolio_relevance: Confirms no double counting: financial-sector holdings either hit the numerator as a deduction or the denominator as RWA, which matters when comparing them against credit card RWA on a like-for-like basis.

R-CAP30.29-significant-investment-defini.title: Definition of a significant investment in an unconsolidated financial entity
R-CAP30.29-significant-investment-defini.statement: The significant investment adjustment applies where the bank owns more than 10% of the issued common share capital of an unconsolidated banking, financial or insurance entity, or where the entity is an affiliate of the bank.
R-CAP30.29-significant-investment-defini.quote: The regulatory adjustment described in this section applies to investments in the capital or other TLAC liabilities of banking, financial and insurance entities that are outside the scope of regulatory consolidation where the bank owns more than 10% of the issued common share capital of the issuing entity or where the entity is an affiliate of the bank.

applies_to.note: Control for affiliate purposes means 20% or more of a class of voting securities, or consolidation for financial reporting.

numeric_values: more than 10% of issued common share capital
R-CAP30.29-significant-investment-defini.portfolio_relevance: Sets the ownership threshold at which a stake in a card-issuing joint venture or fintech partner flips from a threshold item to a full corresponding deduction.

R-CAP30.30-corresponding-deduction-non-c.title: Non-common-share investments in significant holdings fully deducted
R-CAP30.30-corresponding-deduction-non-c.statement: All investments in capital instruments of significant unconsolidated financial holdings that are not common shares must be fully deducted following a corresponding deduction approach, applied to the same tier for which the instrument would qualify if issued by the bank.
R-CAP30.30-corresponding-deduction-non-c.quote: All investments in capital instruments included above that are not common shares must be fully deducted following a corresponding deduction approach.

applies_to.note: Holdings of other TLAC liabilities are fully deducted from Tier 2; shortfalls cascade upward.

R-CAP30.30-corresponding-deduction-non-c.portfolio_relevance: Makes subordinated funding provided to an affiliated finance company a full capital deduction, removing an off-balance-sheet route to expanding consumer credit.

R-CAP30.32-threshold-10pct-each-item.title: Threshold items each capped at 10% of common equity
R-CAP30.32-threshold-10pct-each-item.statement: Instead of full deduction, significant investments in the common shares of unconsolidated financial institutions, mortgage servicing rights, and DTAs arising from temporary differences may each receive limited recognition in CET1, capped at 10% of the bank's common equity.
R-CAP30.32-threshold-10pct-each-item.quote: the following items may each receive limited recognition when calculating Common Equity Tier 1, with recognition capped at 10% of the bank’s common equity

applies_to.note: Measured after applying all regulatory adjustments in CAP30.7 to CAP30.30.

R-CAP30.32-threshold-10pct-each-item.portfolio_relevance: The temporary-difference DTA generated by a large credit card allowance is the item most likely to breach this 10% cap at a small card-heavy bank, converting extra provisioning into an outright CET1 deduction.

R-CAP30.32-three-threshold-items.title: The three threshold deduction items
R-CAP30.32-three-threshold-items.statement: The threshold deduction items are significant investments in the common shares of unconsolidated financial institutions, mortgage servicing rights, and deferred tax assets arising from temporary differences.
R-CAP30.32-three-threshold-items.quote: (1) significant investments in the common shares of unconsolidated financial institutions (banks, insurance and other financial entities) as referred to in CAP30.29; (2) mortgage servicing rights; and (3) DTAs that arise from temporary differences.

applies_to.note: Definition of the specified items subject to both the 10% individual and 15% aggregate caps.

R-CAP30.32-three-threshold-items.portfolio_relevance: Names the exact balance sheet lines that compete with credit RWA for CET1 headroom, two of which (MSRs and allowance-driven DTAs) move directly with lending strategy.

R-CAP30.33-aggregate-15pct-cap.title: Aggregate threshold items capped at 15% of CET1
R-CAP30.33-aggregate-15pct-cap.statement: The amount of the three threshold items that remains recognised after all regulatory adjustments must not exceed 15% of Common Equity Tier 1 capital calculated after all regulatory adjustments.
R-CAP30.33-aggregate-15pct-cap.quote: The amount of the three items that remains recognised after the application of all regulatory adjustments must not exceed 15% of the Common Equity Tier 1 capital, calculated after all regulatory adjustments.

applies_to.note: Operationalised as 17.65% of post-deduction CET1.

R-CAP30.33-aggregate-15pct-cap.portfolio_relevance: An aggregate cap on top of the per-item caps, so a bank simultaneously carrying MSRs and a large card allowance DTA loses CET1 even if neither item alone breaches 10%.

R-CAP30.33-17.65-multiplier.title: The 15% aggregate cap is applied as a 17.65% multiplier
R-CAP30.33-17.65-multiplier.statement: To determine the maximum recognisable amount of the specified items, the 15% aggregate limit is applied as 17.65% of CET1 measured after deducting the specified items in full, derived from 15%/85%.
R-CAP30.33-17.65-multiplier.quote: This number is derived from the proportion of 15% to 85% (ie 15%/85% = 17.65%).

applies_to.note: Computational convention set out in the FAQ to CAP30.33.

R-CAP30.33-17.65-multiplier.portfolio_relevance: Gives the exact arithmetic needed to compute the CET1 deduction from published MSR and DTA balances, making the constraint machine-checkable from filings.

R-CAP30.34-250-risk-weight.title: Non-deducted threshold items risk weighted at 250%
R-CAP30.34-250-risk-weight.statement: The amount of the three threshold items that is not deducted in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1 must be risk weighted at 250%.
R-CAP30.34-250-risk-weight.quote: The amount of the three items that are not deducted in the calculation of Common Equity Tier 1 will be risk weighted at 250%.

applies_to.note: Applies to the recognised portion only; deducted amounts are excluded from RWA.

R-CAP30.34-250-risk-weight.portfolio_relevance: A 250% weight makes retained DTAs and MSRs more RWA-intensive per dollar than an unsecured credit card exposure at 75-100%, so provisioning-driven DTAs crowd out card lending capacity in the denominator as well as the numerator.

R-CAP30.34-dta-tax-credit-100rw.title: DTAs automatically converted to refundable tax credits risk weighted at 100%
R-CAP30.34-dta-tax-credit-100rw.statement: Where a national tax regime automatically transforms DTAs arising from temporary differences into a refundable tax credit if the bank is unprofitable, liquidated or insolvent, banks need not deduct those DTAs and may apply a 100% risk weight.
R-CAP30.34-dta-tax-credit-100rw.quote: No. Banks may apply a 100% risk weight for DTAs arising from temporary differences in such tax regimes.

applies_to.note: Depends on the national tax regime providing automatic conversion and cash refundability; not generally available in the United States or Canada.

R-CAP30.34-dta-tax-credit-100rw.portfolio_relevance: A jurisdiction-dependent relief that cuts the effective cost of allowance-driven DTAs from a deduction plus 250% weight to a plain 100% weight, materially changing the capital cost of aggressive card provisioning.

R-CAP30.2-tlac-scope-gsib-only.title: Minimum TLAC requirements apply only to G-SIBs
R-CAP30.2-tlac-scope-gsib-only.statement: Global systemically important banks are required to meet a minimum total loss-absorbing capacity requirement set in accordance with the FSB TLAC principles and term sheet, and banks investing in TLAC instruments may be required to deduct them.
R-CAP30.2-tlac-scope-gsib-only.quote: Global systemically important banks (G-SIBs) are required to meet a minimum total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) requirement set in accordance with the Financial Stability Board's (FSB) TLAC principles and term sheet.

applies_to.note: Issuance requirement is G-SIB only, but the holdings deduction in CAP30.25 applies to non-G-SIBs as investors.

R-CAP30.2-tlac-scope-gsib-only.portfolio_relevance: Size gate: a small bank never has to issue TLAC, but it is still subject to deductions if it invests in G-SIB TLAC paper as a treasury asset instead of lending.
